title: Distinct affective neural phenotypes in breast cancer survivors: implications for personalized supportive care after chemotherapy.
abstract: Purpose Anxiety and emotional dysregulation remain among the most prevalent unmet supportive care needs in breast cancer survivorship, yet reported affective outcomes are strikingly inconsistent, with some survivors showing elevated distress and others displaying resilience or post-traumatic growth. Because distress screening in survivorship relies almost exclusively on self-report, the neural mechanisms shaping how chemotherapy-exposed survivors perceive and report emotional experience remain poorly understood, limiting mechanism-informed psychosocial support. Methods Forty female breast cancer survivors (27 chemotherapy-treated, 13 non-chemotherapy) and 30 age-matched healthy controls completed a validated face-word emotional Stroop task during functional MRI to probe emotional attention and conflict regulation. Standardized cognitive and affective questionnaires were aggregated into composite indices characterizing each survivor's neurobehavioral profile. Results Chemotherapy-treated survivors showed poorer Stroop accuracy for faces normatively categorized as fearful and hypoactivation of the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, yet reported lower affective symptoms than non-chemotherapy survivors, who instead showed heightened negative attentional bias and greater incongruency-related interference in the parahippocampal gyrus and insula. A normative inverse coupling between dorsal anterior cingulate cortex activation and affective symptom severity was present only in healthy controls. Conclusion Breast cancer survivors exhibit distinct neurobehavioral phenotypes with potential supportive care implications. Lower self-reported distress in chemotherapy-treated survivors paralleled reduced salience network engagement, a configuration compatible with emotional blunting rather than genuine well-being; because emotional blunting was not measured directly, this remains an interpretive hypothesis. These findings caution against relying solely on self-report screening and motivate the hypothesis that treatment-history-informed survivorship care may be beneficial-affective re-engagement strategies for chemotherapy-exposed survivors, and attention-bias modification or mindfulness-based approaches for non-chemotherapy survivors-a proposal that now requires testing in intervention trials.

title: MR spectroscopy in the diagnosis of lumbar discogenic pain.
abstract: Purpose to determine whether magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) provides similar clinical data to low pressure provocative discography (PD). Methods Twenty patients suffering from axial lower back pain underwent both MRS and PD concurrently. MRS was performed on a Siemens 3T scanner* of the lower three lumbar discs, where possible. Collapsed discs could not be assessed. Low pressure PD was performed on at least the lower three discs, by the author with considerable experience of the technique. Results MRS agreed with PD findings in 70-87% of 55 discs tested, depending on the agreement level set. Of the non-agreements, 10/17 were under-calls, 3 were overcalls and 4 were indeterminate. Conclusion MRS of lumbar discs may become a viable alternative to PD, as our experience and the technique evolves.

title: Digital twin validation and predictive value of delta radiomics based on tabular transformer for synergistic muscle imbalance in lumbar disc degeneration.
abstract: Background Current methods struggle to quantify muscle synergistic imbalance and nonlinear interactions in Lumbar Intervertebral Disc Degeneration (LIDD). This study proposes a novel strategy combining "Delta Radiomics" with a Tabular Transformer deep learning architecture, aiming to improve the precision of early risk assessment. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on L4-L5 MRI images from 663 subjects. Texture features of the Psoas Major (PM) and Erector Spinae (ES) were extracted, and (PM-ES)/ES was calculated as the "Delta Feature" to eliminate individual variation. An in silico digital twin simulation system was constructed to validate the physical sensitivity of these features. The predictive performance of the nonlinear Tabular Transformer model was compared with a traditional logistic regression model. Results In silico experiments confirmed that Delta features possess superior "common-mode noise rejection" capabilities. In the early stage of degeneration (Step 20), when original features showed only weak changes, Delta features detected highly significant inter-group differences (P < 0.001). In the independent test set, the Tabular Transformer model demonstrated the best discriminative power with an AUC of 0.848 (95% CI: 0.781-0.916), outperforming the Combined linear model utilizing the same features (AUC = 0.804, P = 0.089) and single-modality models. Although the raw AUC improvement was marginal, Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) and quantitative calibration (Brier score = 0.145) showed that the Transformer model offered higher net clinical benefit and superior absolute risk estimation across a wider threshold range. Additionally, SHAP analysis revealed that the core features identified by the model highly aligned with the biomechanical compensation failure mechanisms set in the simulation, validating the model's decision logic. Conclusion Delta radiomics can sensitively capture microscopic muscle imbalance. Combined with the nonlinear modeling advantages of the Tabular Transformer architecture, this approach provides an objective, interpretable, and quantitative basis for the early non-invasive diagnosis and risk stratification of LIDD.

title: Comparison of navigation and fluoroscopic assisted posterior spinal fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis surgery.
abstract: Purpose Intraoperative navigation is increasingly used in spinal deformity surgery. However, evidence comparing navigated and conventional fluoroscopic-assisted posterior fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis is still heterogeneous and often lacks comprehensive perioperative and recovery data. The aim of this study was to retrospectively compare clinical, radiographic, and perioperative outcomes between CT-navigated and fluoroscopic-assisted posterior spinal fusion in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). Methods We analyzed 71 patients (54 female, 17 male) with AIS treated between 2011 and 2018. Surgical indication was a structural curve with a Cobb angle ≥ 45-50°. 37 patients underwent navigated fusion (Nav+), and 34 had conventional fluoroscopic-assisted fusion (Nav-). Outcome parameters included Cobb angle correction, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, fluoroscopy time, surgical complications, need for intensive care, hospital stay, and revision rates. Statistical analyses used nonparametric (Mann-Whitney, Chi-square) tests, with significance at p < 0.05. Results Preoperative Cobb angle was 70.27° (SD 18.84°, range 45-120°) in Nav + and 68.24° (SD 20.88°, range 45-118°) in Nav-. Mean number of fused segments was higher in Nav+ (10.24 ± 1.77; range 7-14) compared to Nav- (9.26 ± 2.67; range 4-14). Cobb correction did not differ significantly (24.5° vs. 24.7°, p = 0.85). Operative time was longer in Nav+ (230 vs. 175 min, p = 0.0006). ICU admission was more frequent in Nav+ (73% vs. 32.4%, p = 0.0006). Hospital stay was shorter in Nav+ (10 vs. 13 days, p < 0.00001). Conclusion CT-navigation did not improve radiographic correction in AIS. CT-based navigation achieved radiographic correction comparable to fluoroscopic-assisted posterior spinal fusion in AIS. Navigation was associated with longer operative time. Differences in ICU utilization and hospital stay should be interpreted cautiously because they may reflect institutional practice patterns, temporal changes during the study period, surgeon-dependent treatment allocation, and differences in surgical complexity. Level of evidence III, retrospective study.

title: Predurotomy intraoperative ultrasound in intradural extramedullary spinal tumor surgery: agreement with preoperative magnetic resonance imaging and correlation with microsurgical findings.
abstract: Background Intraoperative ultrasound (IOUS) has been widely used in spinal tumor surgery. However, this imaging modality is highly operator-dependent and the available evidence regarding its applications in this field is derived predominantly from descriptive studies, while studies systematically assessing its agreement with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or its correlation with microsurgical findings remain scarce. The present study provides an assessment of the agreement between predurotomy IOUS and preoperative MRI in intradural extramedullary (IDEM) spinal tumor surgery based on an interobserver comparative analysis of several anatomical structures that are consistently identifiable and reproducible in this setting. In addition, corresponding microsurgical images are presented, establishing an integrated MRI-IOUS-Microsurgery correlation framework that may be valuable for both neuroradiologists and neurosurgeons. Methods A retrospective case series of patients with IDEM spinal tumors was compiled. Each case was characterised using a set of representative images depicting the same anatomical area of interest (tumor location), obtained by predurotomy IOUS, preoperative MRI and an operating microscope. Experienced neurosurgeons independently evaluated the IOUS images and MRI scans using a structured questionnaire and rated the perceived agreement on a 5-point scale by comparing several structures. Agreement between predurotomy IOUS and preoperative MRI was subsequently analysed. These structures were identified in an integrated MRI-IOUS-Microsurgery correlation framework. Results Nine patients with IDEM spinal tumors were included. A total of 768 agreement assessments were obtained, of which 579 (75.39%) were comparable. Tumor and spinal cord showed the highest levels of agreement between IOUS and MRI, followed by the subarachnoid space and dura mater, which also showed high, although somewhat lower, agreement. In contrast, pia mater and nerve roots showed the lowest levels of agreement. Compared with MRIT1c, MRIT2 demonstrated significantly higher agreement with IOUS for nerve roots, dura mater, pia mater and subarachnoid space, while there were no significant differences for tumor or spinal cord. Sagittal images achieved significantly higher agreement scores than axial images. Despite systematic differences in scoring among observers, interobserver reliability was good when ratings from four observers were averaged, with comparable reproducibility for IOUS-MRIT1c and IOUS-MRIT2. Conclusions Taking interobserver variability into account, IOUS-MRI agreement varied according to the anatomical structure evaluated, being highest for tumor and spinal cord, followed by subarachnoid space and dura mater, and lowest for pia mater and nerve roots. Sagittal images provided superior anatomical orientation compared with axial images. Interobserver reproducibility remained good despite systematic differences in individual scoring behavior.

title: The LL-TK index as a regional marker of sagittal balance and disability in adults with chronic low back pain.
abstract: Purpose Population aging has increased both the prevalence and clinical impact of adult spinal deformity (ASD). Sagittal and regional parameters (e.g., SVA, PI-LL, LL-TK) guide assessment and treatment planning, but it remains unclear which indices are most closely associated with sagittal imbalance and functional disability. This study therefore evaluated the associations between regional and global spinopelvic parameters and clinical status in an adult outpatient cohort with chronic low back pain, and compared the ability of the LL-TK and PI-LL indices to discriminate concurrent sagittal imbalance. Methods Cross-sectional study including 142 patients (mean age 56.6 ± 13.2 years) with chronic low back pain, evaluated between 2018 and 2019. Standing full-length AP and lateral radiographs were analyzed using Surgimap to measure SVA, LL, TK, PI, PT and SS. Regional indices (LL-TK and PI-LL) were calculated. Patients were classified as balanced (SVA < 4 cm) or unbalanced (SVA ≥ 4 cm). Pearson correlations, independent-samples t tests and ROC analysis were performed; significance threshold p < 0.05. Results Mean values were: ODI 23.6 ± 14.2; VAS 4.5 ± 2.3; LL 55.3° ± 13.0; TK 44.1° ± 13.8; PI 52.8° ± 10.9; PT 16° ± 9.0; SS 36.9° ± 9.0; PI-LL - 2.5° ± 12.8. SVA correlated significantly with age (r = 0.50), ODI (r = 0.40), VAS (r = 0.42), LL (r = - 0.28), LL-TK (r = - 0.43) and PI-LL (r = 0.42) (all p < 0.001). LL-TK also demonstrated significant correlations with clinical and radiographic measures. Twenty-nine patients (20.4%) were sagittally unbalanced. For the identification of concurrent sagittal imbalance, ROC analysis yielded optimal cutoffs of 12° for LL-TK (AUC = 0.755; sensitivity 96.6%; specificity 55.8%) and 9° for PI-LL (AUC = 0.699; sensitivity 44.8%; specificity 86.7%); the AUC of LL-TK was numerically higher, but the two correlated curves were not compared statistically. The combined criterion LL-TK > 12° and PI-LL ≤ 9° was met by 56 patients, of whom 55 (98%) had satisfactory sagittal alignment (SVA < 4 cm). Conversely, LL-TK ≤ 12° combined with PI-LL > 9° identified 14 patients, 11 (78%) of whom were sagittally unbalanced (positive predictive value 78%; negative predictive value of the favorable combination 98%). The remaining 72 patients (50.7%) had discordant index values and were not classified by this rule. Conclusions In this cross-sectional cohort of adults with chronic low back pain, the regional LL-TK index was moderately associated with SVA and with patient-reported disability, and its AUC for discriminating sagittal malalignment was numerically higher than that of PI-LL; the two AUCs were not formally compared, so no superiority is claimed. The combination of regional and pelvic parameters yielded a high predictive values in the concordant subgroups, suggesting potential value as an adjunct screening aid rather than a basis for outcome prediction or surgical planning. Multicenter studies with standardized radiography, bone quality assessment and prospective validation of the proposed thresholds are needed.

Mean values were: ODI 23.6 ± 14.2; VAS 4.5 ± 2.3; LL 55.3° ± 13.0; TK 44.1° ± 13.8; PI 52.8° ± 10.9; PT 16° ± 9.0; SS 36.9° ± 9.0; PI-LL - 2.5° ± 12.8. SVA correlated significantly with age (r = 0.50), ODI (r = 0.40), VAS (r = 0.42), LL (r = - 0.28), LL-TK (r = - 0.43) and PI-LL (r = 0.42) (all p < 0.001). LL-TK also demonstrated significant correlations with clinical and radiographic measures. Twenty-nine patients (20.4%) were sagittally unbalanced. For the identification of concurrent sagittal imbalance, ROC analysis yielded optimal cutoffs of 12° for LL-TK (AUC = 0.755; sensitivity 96.6%; specificity 55.8%) and 9° for PI-LL (AUC = 0.699; sensitivity 44.8%; specificity 86.7%); the AUC of LL-TK was numerically higher, but the two correlated curves were not compared statistically. The combined criterion LL-TK > 12° and PI-LL ≤ 9° was met by 56 patients, of whom 55 (98%) had satisfactory sagittal alignment (SVA < 4 cm). Conversely, LL-TK ≤ 12° combined with PI-LL > 9° identified 14 patients, 11 (78%) of whom were sagittally unbalanced (positive predictive value 78%; negative predictive value of the favorable combination 98%). The remaining 72 patients (50.7%) had discordant index values and were not classified by this rule.

Conclusions

In this cross-sectional cohort of adults with chronic low back pain, the regional LL-TK index was moderately associated with SVA and with patient-reported disability, and its AUC for discriminating sagittal malalignment was numerically higher than that of PI-LL; the two AUCs were not formally compared, so no superiority is claimed. The combination of regional and pelvic parameters yielded a high predictive values in the concordant subgroups, suggesting potential value as an adjunct screening aid rather than a basis for outcome prediction or surgical planning. Multicenter studies with standardized radiography, bone quality assessment and prospective validation of the proposed thresholds are needed.

title: Association of pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration with early postoperative hemostasis in patients undergoing head-pelvic ring traction and three-column osteotomy for severe spinal deformity: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Severe spinal deformity correction is associated with substantial perioperative blood loss. Evidence on pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration in this setting remains limited. This study evaluated whether pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated with more favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 50 patients with severe spinal deformity who underwent head-pelvic ring traction followed by corrective surgery. Patients were classified into a fibrinogen group and a non-fibrinogen group according to whether they received pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration. Postoperative coagulation parameters, hemoglobin (Hb) levels, drainage volume, and radiographic correction outcomes were compared between groups. Results Twenty-five patients were included in each group. Baseline characteristics, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and radiographic correction outcomes were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-fibrinogen group, the fibrinogen group had lower postoperative prothrombin time and international normalized ratio, and higher prothrombin activity and fibrinogen levels (all P < 0.01). Hb levels on postoperative days 1 and 3 were higher in the fibrinogen group, whereas postoperative drainage volume and postoperative red blood cell transfusion volume were lower (P = 0.002, 0.036, 0.005, and < 0.001, respectively). No significant between-group difference was observed in Hb level on postoperative day 7. Conclusions Pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated with more favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters in patients undergoing corrective surgery for severe spinal deformity. Given the retrospective design and potential residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospective studies.

title: Accuracy of general-purpose large language models (LLMS) in interpreting adolescent idiopathic scoliosis radiographs: a comparative study with experienced spine surgeons.
abstract: Purpose This study evaluates the accuracy of general-purpose, vision-capable large language models (LLMs) in interpreting adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) radiographs and compares their outputs with an expert surgeon consensus reference standard. Methods This retrospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study analyzed 128 anonymized AIS radiographic case sets from 128 different patients, including standing coronal and sagittal radiographs and lateral bending films. ChatGPT GPT-5.2 Instant, Gemini 3 Flash, and Grok 4.1 were evaluated through their official web interfaces in January 2026 using the original standardized prompt based on the Lenke classification system. Model inputs were de-identified raw radiographs without measurement lines, Cobb values, vertebral labels, or Surgimap overlays. Three spine surgeons with more than 10 years of deformity surgery experience independently assessed all cases using Surgimap. Surgeon consensus was the reference standard. Cobb angle (CA) accuracy was assessed using mean absolute error and agreement within ± 5°; categorical variables were assessed by exact agreement with 95% confidence intervals. Results ChatGPT achieved 94.5% agreement within ± 5° of surgeon consensus, with a mean absolute CA error of 2.4°. Gemini achieved 92.2% agreement with a mean absolute error of 2.7°, and Grok achieved 90.6% agreement with a mean absolute error of 3.1°. Exact agreement was substantially lower for Lenke classification, lumbar and sagittal modifiers, neutral vertebra, and stable vertebra identification. Inter-rater reliability among surgeons was high for CA and categorical parameters. No formal inferential ranking between LLMs was performed. Conclusion The tested general-purpose LLM versions showed limited reliability for comprehensive AIS radiographic interpretation. Their performance was substantially weaker for Lenke classification, modifiers, and fusion-level-related landmarks than for CA estimation. The findings do not support independent use of these systems for scoliosis measurement, education, or surgical planning. At present, these tools should be regarded as supervised documentation or teaching aids rather than measurement or decision-making systems.

title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
abstract: Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges. Methods A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation. Results Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation. Conclusion AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

title: Modic changes, chronic low back pain, and lifestyle and mental health factors: a cross-sectional analysis of a cohort study.
abstract: Purpose Modic changes (MC) are vertebral endplate and adjacent bone marrow MRI findings that have been associated with chronic low back pain (CLBP), although their clinical relevance remains debated. This study examined whether MC presence and extent are associated with CLBP status, pain intensity, and disability, and whether lifestyle or mental health factors moderate the MC-pain relationship. Methods This exploratory cross-sectional sub-study included 239 adults: 135 with CLBP and 104 controls without. Lumbar MRI scans were evaluated for MC presence, type, craniocaudal extent of vertebral body involvement, and transverse extent of endplate involvement. Firth penalized logistic regression examined associations of MC presence, type and extent with CLBP status. Linear regression models examined associations between aggregated MC count and vertebral body and endplate extent with low back pain intensity and disability within CLBP and control groups. Moderation analyses tested whether sleep disturbance, physical activity, anxiety, depression, or pain catastrophizing modified the association between MC count and low back pain intensity among individuals with CLBP. All models were adjusted for age, sex, smoking, and body mass index. Results Any MC were associated with higher odds of CLBP (OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.45-4.30; p = 0.001), with similar associations for Type 1 and Type 2 MC. Greater vertebral body involvement showed a graded association with CLBP, with > 50% vertebral body involvement associated with the highest odds (OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.14-20.92; p = 0.033). Among individuals with CLBP, aggregated MC count (β = 0.30, 95% CI 0.05-0.55; p = 0.019) and vertebral body extent (β = 0.11, 95% CI 0.01-0.21; p = 0.039) were associated with higher pain intensity, but not disability. Endplate extent was not associated with pain or disability. None of the examined lifestyle or psychological factors significantly moderated the MC-pain association. Conclusion This exploratory analysis revealed that MC, particularly those with greater vertebral body involvement, were associated with CLBP status and low back pain intensity. Lifestyle and psychological factors were related to pain severity but did not significantly modify the MC-pain relationship. These findings suggest that MC extent may be a clinically relevant imaging characteristic, although longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causality and prognostic significance.

title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
abstract: Introduction Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis. Results The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%). Conclusion Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonist use and contrast-associated acute kidney injury after contrast-enhanced CT and CT angiography in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease: a propensity score-matched cohort study.
abstract: Aims To examine whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use is associated with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CE-CT) or computed tomographic angiography (CTA) in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods We conducted a TriNetX retrospective cohort study of adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD who underwent CE-CT or CTA from January 2020 to January 2025. GLP-1 RA use was defined by a prescription within six months before imaging. The primary outcome was a new acute kidney injury diagnosis within three days. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched analyses were conducted for CE-CT and CTA, with eGFR-stratified and sensitivity analyses. Results After matching, the CE-CT and CTA cohorts included 6,995 and 3,285 pairs, respectively. CA-AKI occurred in 3.8% of GLP-1 RA users versus 4.5% of non-users after CE-CT (odds ratio [OR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.71-0.99) and in 4.5% versus 6.1% after CTA (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.92). The absolute risk differences were 0.7% points and 1.5% points, respectively. HbA1c remained imbalanced after matching. Negative-control outcomes were null, and eGFR-stratified associations were inconsistent between cohorts. Conclusions GLP-1 RA use was associated with a lower observed risk of CA-AKI after CE-CT and CTA in adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD. Residual HbA1c imbalance and the observational design limit causal interpretation; prospective studies using creatinine-based outcomes are needed.

Aims

To examine whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) use is associated with contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CE-CT) or computed tomographic angiography (CTA) in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD).

We conducted a TriNetX retrospective cohort study of adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD who underwent CE-CT or CTA from January 2020 to January 2025. GLP-1 RA use was defined by a prescription within six months before imaging. The primary outcome was a new acute kidney injury diagnosis within three days. Separate 1:1 propensity score-matched analyses were conducted for CE-CT and CTA, with eGFR-stratified and sensitivity analyses.

After matching, the CE-CT and CTA cohorts included 6,995 and 3,285 pairs, respectively. CA-AKI occurred in 3.8% of GLP-1 RA users versus 4.5% of non-users after CE-CT (odds ratio [OR] 0.84, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.71-0.99) and in 4.5% versus 6.1% after CTA (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.59-0.92). The absolute risk differences were 0.7% points and 1.5% points, respectively. HbA1c remained imbalanced after matching. Negative-control outcomes were null, and eGFR-stratified associations were inconsistent between cohorts.

Conclusions

GLP-1 RA use was associated with a lower observed risk of CA-AKI after CE-CT and CTA in adults with type 2 diabetes and CKD. Residual HbA1c imbalance and the observational design limit causal interpretation; prospective studies using creatinine-based outcomes are needed.

title: Neurofilaments support the differentiation of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis from degenerative cervical myelopathy.
abstract: The differential diagnosis between degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and early amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is often clinically challenging; laboratory tests that support this distinction could be highly valuable. This study examined the concentrations of neurofilament light chain (NfL) and the phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNfH), in CSF and serum of carefully selected patients with DCM, spinal canal stenosis (SCS) and ALS, after exclusion of major neurological confounders. Patients were assigned to five groups according to MRI findings and ALS diagnosis. All patients were treated in the Department of Neurology, and were only included if a CSF or serum sample was available for retrospective measurement of neurofilaments. Z-scores were used for age-adjusted interpretation of NfL concentrations in CSF and serum. In addition, the albumin quotient (QAlb), as a marker for the integrity of the blood-CSF barrier, was investigated in the five patient groups. The levels of NfL and pNfH, including Z-score distributions, differed significantly. The groups with diagnosed ALS had elevated neurofilaments both in CSF and Serum. Comparison of neurofilament concentrations between patients with isolated spinal canal stenosis and patients with cervical myelopathy revealed no significant difference. The QAlb showed no clear correlation with elevated neurofilaments and provided limited value for differential diagnosis. In summary, we showed that NfL and pNfH in CSF and serum support the differential diagnosis of cervical SCS with and without myelopathy from ALS in carefully selected cohorts. However, since neurofilaments are not specific, they should be used in context with clinical assessment and imaging for individual diagnostic and treatment decisions.

title: Twenty-five years of progress in Parkinson's disease research: from dopamine replacement to biological definition and regenerative therapy.
abstract: The first quarter of the twenty-first century has transformed Parkinson's disease (PD) from a predominantly motor, dopamine-deficiency syndrome into a heterogeneous multisystem disorder defined across clinical, genetic and molecular dimensions. This overview follows the trajectory of these advances from the historical foundations established prior 2000 to present concepts of prodromal disease, progression, biological classification and precision medicine. Epidemiological work has established PD as the fastest-growing major neurological disorder, while systematic characterization of non-motor symptoms has shifted diagnosis and attention beyond the nigrostriatal system in PD research. Imaging has progressed from exclusionary structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to quantitative susceptibility, diffusion and molecular approaches, although no single imaging biomarker yet provides a stand-alone diagnosis of PD. The discovery of α-synuclein gene mutations and its presence as protein in Lewy bodies and neurites connected genetics, protein aggregation and selective neuronal vulnerability. Seed amplification assays (SAA) now enable robust detection of pathological α-synuclein in cerebrospinal fluid and have catalysed biologically anchored staging proposals. At the same time, negative phase 2 antibody against α-synuclein trials illustrate the challenges of target engagement, disease heterogeneity and intervention timing. Genetics and cell biology have placed lysosomal proteostasis, in particular glucocerebrosidase 1 (GBA1) dependent pathways, at the center of disease-modification strategies. Dopaminergic therapy remains extraordinarily effective symptomatically, with continuous delivery systems extending its utility for intermediate and late stages of the disease, whereas cell replacement has re-entered clinical development through standardized pluripotent-stem-cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic progenitors. The next phase of PD research will depend less on a single unifying mechanism than on integrating molecular state, the pattern of neuronal injury, clinical phenotype and individual trajectory to select the right intervention at the right biological stage.

title: Modality-specific quantitative radiologic characterization of diffuse sclerosing osteomyelitis of the mandible: a pilot study.
abstract: Objectives Diffuse sclerosing osteomyelitis (DSO) of the mandible is a rare chronic inflammatory disease characterized by recurrent painful swelling and trismus. While advanced stages are known to show radiographically evident bone sclerosis, objective quantitative imaging criteria remain poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize modality-specific radiological features of DSO using intra-individual side-to-side comparison of bone density and cortical thickness. Materials and methods This single-center retrospective study included 22 patients treated for DSO between 2010 and 2021. Pre-treatment panoramic radiographs were available for all patients, CT datasets for 6 patients, and CBCT for 3 patients. Bone density was quantified using relative grayscale values in panoramic radiography, Hounsfield units (HU) in CT, and gray values in CBCT. Cortical thickness was measured on CT using standardized regions of interest, with contralateral-side comparison. Two blinded observers performed all measurements. Results Quantitative analysis demonstrated significantly higher bone density on the affected side in panoramic radiography and CT (panoramic: 46.0 ± 4.0% vs. 39.0 ± 3.6%, p < 0.001; CT: 1220.9 ± 215.8 HU vs. 1108.0 ± 163.9 HU, p = 0.01). In the three available CBCT datasets, descriptively higher gray values were observed on the affected side. CT analysis revealed significantly increased cortical thickness (5.63 ± 0.96 mm vs. 3.86 ± 0.75 mm, p = 0.04). A blurred inferior alveolar nerve canal was consistently observed on panoramic radiographs. Conclusions Quantitative side-to-side assessment provides an objective radiological description of DSO and may support imaging assessment when interpreted together with clinical and histopathological findings. Clinical relevance In this selected cohort, DSO-affected regions showed relative densification, cortical thickening in the available CT examinations, and blurring of the inferior alveolar nerve canal on panoramic radiographs.

title: Management of dental-origin gastrointestinal foreign bodies: a proposed site-based, risk-stratified framework for multidisciplinary care.
abstract: Objectives To propose a risk-stratified, site-specific framework tailored to the biomechanical hazards of dental-origin gastrointestinal foreign bodies (DGIFBs). Materials and methods We conducted a narrative review with expert consensus-based synthesis, evaluating leading gastroenterological and surgical consensus statements on aerodigestive and gastrointestinal emergencies. Dedicated guidelines for DGIFBs are currently scarce. Consequently, we systematically extrapolated management principles for sharp, complex objects and integrated them with clinical data on dental device complications. Results DGIFBs (e.g., endodontic files, prostheses) possess sharp, rigid morphologies that inherently increase the mechanical risk of perforation and mediastinitis compared to blunt objects. The proposed algorithms are derived from extrapolated evidence rather than prospectively validated recommendations. By adapting generic guidelines to dental device morphologies, the extrapolated framework supports emergent endoscopic assessment and retrieval (within 2-6 h) for pharyngeal and esophageal DGIFBs. Gastric and proximal small bowel impactions warrant urgent extraction (< 24 h) if the object is sharp or exceeds 6 cm in length or 2.5 cm in diameter. Distal intestinal DGIFBs require serial radiologic monitoring, and surgical consultation/intervention should be considered when a sharp object fails to progress over approximately 3 days, particularly in the presence of symptoms or imaging evidence of complications. Plain radiography serves as the primary screening tool, with an immediate transition to CT for radiolucent materials or suspected extraluminal migration. Conclusions DGIFBs represent a high-morbidity subset of foreign bodies. Their management requires a departure from generic conservative observation in favor of rapid risk stratification, supporting timely endoscopic or surgical assessment of high-risk objects while avoiding prolonged conservative observation when established risk criteria are present. Clinical relevance This review highlights the need for primary prevention. Routine rubber dam isolation is an important practice in dental care. The proposed pathway promotes teamwork between dentistry, emergency medicine, gastroenterology, and surgery. This helps improve patient safety and reduce severe complications.

title: Atypical Stafne bone defect: a systematic review.
abstract: Objectives Atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs) may be challenging to identify because they deviate from the typical posterior mandibular presentation. This systematic review aims to analyze and synthesize the radiographic, anatomical, and histological characteristics of atypically located SBDs reported in the literature and to assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Materials and methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science databases up to January 2026. Eligibility criteria included English-language case reports and case series describing atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs). Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using an adapted assessment tool for case reports. Results Seventy studies encompassing 91 atypical cases were included. Atypically located SBDs were most frequently reported in the anterior mandible. Despite their variable localization, these defects share key anatomical and radiographic features with classical SBDs, including well-defined unilocular radiolucencies and lingual cortical depressions. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), play an important role in confirming these features and in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Histological analysis, when available, most commonly revealed normal salivary gland tissue without evidence of neoplastic transformation. Conclusions Atypically located SBDs demonstrate consistent radiographic and anatomical characteristics that may assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. This review improves the understanding of this under-recognized anatomical variant and highlights the importance of appropriate imaging evaluation in ambiguous cases. Clinical relevance Recognition of these features may facilitate accurate diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Validation of 3D intraoral scanner use for detecting caries lesions around dental restorations: A diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to validate the use of a 3D intraoral scanner (IOS) for detecting secondary caries lesions around restorations using image-based CARS-derived severity categories, compared with visual-tactile clinical examination. Materials and methods A diagnostic validation study was conducted at the university clinical facilities, from July 2023 to September 2024, including adult patients with amalgam or composite resin restorations on anterior and posterior teeth. The restorations were assessed using visual-tactile clinical examination, adopted as the clinical reference standard, and IOS image-based assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, binary-classification AUC, and clinical-IOS agreement were estimated. Confidence intervals for diagnostic accuracy measures were obtained using participant-level cluster bootstrap resampling. Results A total of 299 restorations in 41 patients were assessed. IOS sensitivity varied, with 75% (95% CI: 66.2-82.0) at the initial lesion threshold, 40% (95% CI: 20.8-57.7) at the moderate lesion threshold, and 57.1% (95% CI: 33.3-100.0) at the severe lesion threshold. Specificity was consistently high, with 84.1% (95% CI: 78.7-89.4), 97.4% (95% CI: 95.6-99.2), and 99.7% (95% CI: 98.7-99.7) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Binary-classification AUC values were 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.84), 0.69 (95% CI: 0.58-0.78), and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.66-1.00) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Positive predictive value was highest at the severe lesion threshold (80%), while the negative predictive value was especially high at this threshold (99%). Exact clinical-IOS agreement was 77.9%, whereas linearly weighted observed agreement was 91.1%, with a linearly weighted kappa coefficient of 0.53. Conclusions The 3D intraoral scanner is a complementary tool for assessing secondary caries lesions, showing high specificity across lesion thresholds. Sensitivity varied according to lesion severity and was less precise at the severe threshold due to the small number of severe lesions. Future research should increase sample sizes and explore combining IOS with other diagnostic methods to improve detection, especially for moderate lesions and higher caries prevalence. Clinical relevance Conventional IOS images may assist in documenting and assessing visible changes around restorations. Clinical interpretation should consider the observed sensitivity limitations and incorporate visual-tactile examination and radiographic assessment when indicated.

Specificity was consistently high, with 84.1% (95% CI: 78.7-89.4), 97.4% (95% CI: 95.6-99.2), and 99.7% (95% CI: 98.7-99.7) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Binary-classification AUC values were 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.84), 0.69 (95% CI: 0.58-0.78), and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.66-1.00) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Positive predictive value was highest at the severe lesion threshold (80%), while the negative predictive value was especially high at this threshold (99%). Exact clinical-IOS agreement was 77.9%, whereas linearly weighted observed agreement was 91.1%, with a linearly weighted kappa coefficient of 0.53.

Conclusions

The 3D intraoral scanner is a complementary tool for assessing secondary caries lesions, showing high specificity across lesion thresholds. Sensitivity varied according to lesion severity and was less precise at the severe threshold due to the small number of severe lesions. Future research should increase sample sizes and explore combining IOS with other diagnostic methods to improve detection, especially for moderate lesions and higher caries prevalence.

Clinical relevance

Conventional IOS images may assist in documenting and assessing visible changes around restorations. Clinical interpretation should consider the observed sensitivity limitations and incorporate visual-tactile examination and radiographic assessment when indicated.

title: Selective preoperative lower extremity computed tomography angiography before mandibular reconstruction: Identifying patients unlikely to require fibula free flap reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose Not every patient undergoing mandibular continuity resection requires free fibula flap (FFF) reconstruction. Whether clinical judgment reliably identifies patients unlikely to benefit from preoperative lower-extremity computed tomography angiography (CTA) remains unknown, despite the relevance of this question for cost-conscious and resource-efficient imaging strategies. Methods A retrospective outcome-based validation was conducted in patients undergoing mandibular continuity resection between July 2012 and June 2023. The primary outcome was secondary FFF reconstruction among patients not initially selected for CTA. Factors associated with CTA utilization were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Results 316 consecutively operated patients were included. Prior radiotherapy (OR 2.67, p = 0.005) and smoking history (OR 1.98, p = 0.032) were independently associated with CTA utilization. Among 111 patients without primary FFF reconstruction, four (3.6%) required secondary FFF reconstruction, all of whom had undergone CTA. No patient managed without CTA subsequently required FFF reconstruction. Conclusions In this cohort, clinical judgment was associated with successful identification of patients who did not subsequently require fibular reconstruction. Omission of CTA in carefully selected patients was not associated with subsequent reconstructive deficiency, though larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Germinoma in late adulthood with extensive dissemination: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS GCTs) are exceptionally rare in patients aged 60 years or older. We report a 61-year-old man with progressive weight loss and endocrine dysfunction over 20 months, in whom magnetic resonance imaging revealed enhancing lesions including the suprasellar and sellar regions, optic tracts, ventricular walls, corpus callosum, and dorsal medulla. Biopsy findings supported a diagnosis of germinoma in the sampled tissue, and DNA methylation profiling demonstrated a molecular profile consistent with conventional germinoma. The patient underwent whole ventricular irradiation and carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy. Febrile neutropenia during the first cycle required subsequent etoposide dose reductions, but he achieved marked radiographic regression. A descriptive review identified five cases, including the present case, for which sufficient individual clinicopathological information was available. This case highlights that CNS GCTs in older adults may radiologically mimic primary CNS lymphoma and that integrated pathological assessment, including morphology and immunohistochemistry, is essential for diagnosis. In this diagnostically challenging presentation, DNA methylation profiling provided complementary molecular support for the histopathological diagnosis of conventional germinoma.

title: Volumetric analysis of thalamic nuclei in children with vasovagal syncope.
abstract: Aim This study aimed to investigate regional thalamic nuclei volumes in pediatric patients with vasovagal syncope (VVS) using automated MRI-based segmentation and compare these measurements with those of pediatric controls. Materials and methods This retrospective case-control study included 76 pediatric patients with VVS and 34 age- and sex-comparable controls (total n = 110) who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging. Thalamic nuclei were segmented using the FreeSurfer automated pipeline. Group differences were assessed using multivariate and univariate analyses of covariance adjusted for age, sex, and total intracranial volume. False discovery rate correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Results Total right, left, and bilateral thalamic volumes did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.802, P = 0.267, and P = 0.366, respectively). However, significant regional volumetric differences were identified in selected nuclei. Compared with controls, patients with VVS had larger left medial thalamic (P < 0.001), left pulvinar (P < 0.001), right pulvinar (P < 0.001), and right habenular (P < 0.001) volumes, and smaller right anterior ventral (P = 0.004), left mediodorsal (P = 0.003), and left intralaminar/midline (P = 0.012) volumes. After false discovery rate correction, corresponding q values were < 0.001, < 0.001, < 0.001, 0.002, 0.018, 0.017, and 0.043, respectively. Conclusion Children with VVS demonstrated regional volumetric differences in specific thalamic nuclei despite preserved total thalamic volume. The clinical and functional significance of these findings and their potential relationship to autonomic regulation remain uncertain. Further prospective studies incorporating functional and multimodal neuroimaging are warranted.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient.
abstract: Background Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement. Case presentation We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. Her condition deteriorated to focal and dyscognitive status epilepticus, requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI showed imaging features consistent with rhombencephalitis. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed through positive qRT-PCR results from both nasopharyngeal swab and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Further analysis of the CSF using quantitative shotgun proteomics via mass spectrometry revealed a neuroinflammatory profile indicative of blood-brain barrier disruption and differential expression of several proteins relevant to brain function, including the major prion protein, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD-1), and other aggregation-prone proteins. Conclusions This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 can invade the central nervous system and cause severe neurological impairment, even in the absence of typical respiratory symptoms. The findings underscore the importance of considering SARS-CoV-2 in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of neuroinvasion and the potential neurotropism of emerging viral variants.

title: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: from diagnosis to rehabilitation.
abstract: Background Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE) is the second most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, involving physical medicine and rehabilitation, neurology, orthopedics, and plastic surgery. It results from static or dynamic ulnar nerve instability, cubital tunnel syndrome, or space-occupying lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires thorough history, clinical examination, and selection of appropriate diagnostic tests. Search strategy PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (January 2000-August 2026) using combinations of "ulnar neuropathy", "cubital tunnel syndrome", "elbow", "ultrasound", "electrodiagnosis", "conservative treatment", "rehabilitation" and "surgery". English-language original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were eligible; case reports were included only where no higher-level evidence existed. Approximately 220 records were screened; 58 were retained, following SANRA recommendations for narrative reviews. Discussion High-resolution ultrasound provides dynamic, non-invasive, cost-effective evaluation of the ulnar nerve and real-time assessment of compression or instability, and guides minimally invasive procedures such as perineural injections, although the only randomized placebo-controlled trial did not show superiority of corticosteroid injection over placebo. Conservative treatment is usually first-line, although surgery may be required in advanced or refractory cases; comparative evidence shows no clear superiority among surgical techniques, while endoscopic decompression carries a higher complication rate than open approaches. Conclusions This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic pathways and therapeutic options for UNE, highlighting the role of ultrasound as both a diagnostic and interventional tool, and outlines gaps in the literature regarding standardized conservative and surgical protocols.

Background

Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE) is the second most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, involving physical medicine and rehabilitation, neurology, orthopedics, and plastic surgery. It results from static or dynamic ulnar nerve instability, cubital tunnel syndrome, or space-occupying lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires thorough history, clinical examination, and selection of appropriate diagnostic tests.

Search strategy

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (January 2000-August 2026) using combinations of "ulnar neuropathy", "cubital tunnel syndrome", "elbow", "ultrasound", "electrodiagnosis", "conservative treatment", "rehabilitation" and "surgery". English-language original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were eligible; case reports were included only where no higher-level evidence existed. Approximately 220 records were screened; 58 were retained, following SANRA recommendations for narrative reviews.

Discussion

High-resolution ultrasound provides dynamic, non-invasive, cost-effective evaluation of the ulnar nerve and real-time assessment of compression or instability, and guides minimally invasive procedures such as perineural injections, although the only randomized placebo-controlled trial did not show superiority of corticosteroid injection over placebo. Conservative treatment is usually first-line, although surgery may be required in advanced or refractory cases; comparative evidence shows no clear superiority among surgical techniques, while endoscopic decompression carries a higher complication rate than open approaches.

Conclusions

This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic pathways and therapeutic options for UNE, highlighting the role of ultrasound as both a diagnostic and interventional tool, and outlines gaps in the literature regarding standardized conservative and surgical protocols.

title: First report of proven Fusarium brachygibbosum sinusitis in a paediatric patient with acute myeloblastic leukaemia.
abstract: Purpose Fusarium brachygibbosum is an environmental mould belonging to the Fusarium sambucinum species complex (FSAMSC) and is only exceptionally reported as a human pathogen. Invasive fusariosis is a recognized complication in patients with hematological malignancies; however, proven infection caused by F. brachygibbosum has not previously been described. We report the first case of proven breakthrough sinusitis in a pediatric female with refractory acute myeloblastic leukaemia (AML) receiving posaconazole prophylaxis. Methods We describe the clinical presentation, microbiological diagnosis, antifungal susceptibility profile, treatment, and outcome of a 13-year-old neutropenic female with refractory AML who developed invasive fungal sinusitis. Species identification was established by Sanger sequencing of the elongation factor 1-alpha, and antifungal susceptibility testing was performed according to the EUCAST reference method. Results Computed tomography revealed extensive paranasal sinus involvement, and direct microscopy of sinus tissue demonstrated hyaline septate hyphae. Culture yielded a mould initially misidentified by MALDI-TOF MS as F. chlamydosporium. Molecular sequencing confirmed F. brachygibbosum. The isolate exhibited elevated Minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) to amphotericin B, azoles, echinocandins, and olorofim, while fosmanogepix showed a lower in vitro MIC. Extensive surgical debridement combined with liposomal amphotericin B, voriconazole, and subsequently olorofim was performed. Despite local control of the sinonasal infection and no microbiological or histopathological evidence of dissemination, the patient died 23 days after diagnosis. The death occurred in the context of progressive refractory AML, invasive fungal disease, pulmonary abnormalities, and subsequent neutropenic complications. Conclusion This report represents the first proven pediatric case of invasive sinusitis caused by F. brachygibbosum (FSAMSC) isolate with higher MICs to classical antifungals. The case highlights the diagnostic limitations of MALDI-TOF MS for rare Fusarium species, the value of molecular identification and antifungal susceptibility testing, and the emergence of environmental moulds breakthrough fungal infections. It also underscores the urgent need for effective novel antifungal agents against resistant Fusarium species.

title: Screening strategies for the early detection of non-cardia gastric cancer in low- to moderate-prevalence regions: Asia-Pacific gastroesophageal cancer congress consensus 2026.
abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden, and early detection is essential for improving patient outcomes. Although GC screening has been widely implemented in East Asian countries with a high disease burden, the optimal screening strategy for low- to moderate-prevalence regions remains unclear. To address this gap, the Asia Pacific Gastroesophageal Cancer Congress (APGCC) convened an international consensus meeting to develop evidence-based recommendations for improving the detection of non-cardia gastric cancer (NCGC). Methods The APGCC working group developed 11 clinical questions (CQs) addressing GC screening, with a particular focus on NCGC. For each CQ, assigned authors conducted literature reviews using PubMed and prepared evidence summaries and draft recommendations. Consensus was achieved through a two-round modified Delphi process involving 37 international voting members. Results The consensus recommendations addressed population-based screening, screening modalities, identification of high-risk individuals, quality indicators for esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), image-enhanced endoscopy, and artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopy. Population-based endoscopic screening is not recommended in low- to moderate-prevalence regions because of insufficient evidence. However, if screening is performed, EGD is preferred over upper gastrointestinal series for the detection of early NCGC in asymptomatic individuals. The recommendations also emphasize the importance of high-quality endoscopic examinations, risk-stratified screening using serum biomarkers, and the appropriate integration of advanced endoscopic technologies. Conclusions These APGCC consensus recommendations provide practical guidance for improving the early detection of NCGC in low- to moderate-prevalence regions. This consensus also highlights important evidence gaps and establishes a framework for future research and the development of region-specific GC screening strategies.

title: A preoperative risk-scoring model for predicting intraoperative hemorrhage during endoscopic submucosal dissection for gastric neoplasms.
abstract: Background Intraoperative hemorrhage is the most frequent complication of endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). We aim to develop and externally validate a preoperative risk-scoring model for predicting intraoperative hemorrhage during ESD for gastric neoplasms. Methods Patients who underwent ESD for gastric neoplasms from four endoscopy centers were enrolled in this retrospective study, with 1123 patients in derivation cohort and 345 patients in validation cohort. In derivation cohort, univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis were used to identify independent preoperative predictors of intraoperative hemorrhage. A risk-scoring model was created by assigning weighted points to selected predictors. External validation was conducted to analyse the discrimination and calibration of the prediction model. Results A prediction model for intraoperative hemorrhage included 5 variables: upper-third location (5 points), large lesion size (≥ 25 mm) (4 points), current HP infection (3 points), junior endoscopist (3 points) and middle-third location (2 points). Patients were stratified into low- (0-2 points), intermediate- (3-4 points), high- (5-6 points), and very high-risk (≥ 7 points) groups, with corresponding bleeding rates of 4.8%, 35.9%, 80.2% and 98.5%, respectively. In external validation cohort, the model showed excellent discrimination, with a c-statistic of 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.98), and good calibration (calibration-in-the-large, - 0.04; calibration slope, 0.94). Conclusions We developed a preoperative risk-scoring model to predict intraoperative hemorrhage of ESD for gastric neoplasms. For lesions of large size or located on the upper-third of the stomach, ESD should be performed by senior endoscopists after successful HP eradication to minimize the occurrence of bleeding.

title: A comprehensive analysis of the association of psychological profiling and sagittal balance parameters with neck pain in a non-deformity cervical spondylosis population: A prospective two-centers cross-sectional study.
abstract: Purpose to comprehensively identify determining factors of perceived neck pain in a non-deformity population, integrating psychological and sagittal balance parameters.Methods a cross-sectional study of prospectively collected data was conducted on patients admitted for cervical spondylosis at two tertiary university hospitals between April 2024 and August 2025. Eligible cases were retrieved from the PANDA Registry. Records were excluded if standing X-ray was unavailable and/or not-evaluable (e.g. shoulder prosthesis); or if the admission pathology involved the cranio-cervical junction, tumors, deformities, spinal cord disease, or infections. Preoperative data included demographic, clinical (VAS neck), psychological (SCL-27, I-TIPI, CD-RISC10), and sagittal balance variables (McGregor slope, C1-C2 lordosis, C2 slope, C2-C7 lordosis, cSVA, T1 slope, cervical mismatch). Correction for multiple comparisons was applied within pre-specified hypothesis domains.Results one-hundred-thirty records were included. Intra-rater reliability for radiographic parameters was excellent (> 0.9). After categorization of patients by neck pain severity, pairwise analysis showed that only C1-C2 lordosis remained significantly higher in patients exhibiting severe neck pain (VAS < 7 vs. VAS ≥ 7). When stratified for moderate-to-severe neck pain (VAS ≥ 4), several SCL-27 scales, namely dysthymic, vegetative, agoraphobic, sociophobic, and GSI scores, and C1C2 lordosis showed significant differences. Correlation analysis using VAS neck as the dependent variable demonstrated a significant positive correlation with SCL-27 dysthymic and vegetative scores. C1-C2 lordosis showed a significant inverse correlation with neck pain. In univariate analysis, only SCL-27 dysthymic, vegetative, and GSI scores emerged as significant univariate associations of VAS neck. After correction for multiple comparisons, the SCL-27 vegetative, dysthymic and GSI scores retained significance, whereas C1-C2 lordosis did not.Conclusion in a non-deformity population, sagittal balance parameters alone do not adequately explain patient-perceived neck pain. These findings support the preoperative use of psychological assessments, especially the SCL-27, as a useful tool in preoperative screening and individualised counselling.

title: Predictive factors associated with interval changes in STN-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative CT.
abstract: Background Brain shift during deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery may contribute to changes in lead position. Although intracranial air volume is considered an important factor, other intraoperative factors may also influence lead displacement. This study evaluated interval changes in subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative computed tomography (CT) and investigated factors associated with these changes, including intracranial air volume and intraoperative head position. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 42 DBS leads implanted bilaterally in the STN of 21 patients with Parkinson's disease. Lead-tip coordinates were assessed using Elements software (Brainlab) on CT obtained immediately after implantation and after resolution of intracranial air. Interval displacement was defined as the difference in lead-tip coordinates between the delayed and immediate postoperative CT scans. Intraoperative head position was quantified as "Angle A," measured from the horizontal reference line to the anterior commissure-posterior commissure line. Associations between potential explanatory factors and lead-tip displacement were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with patient included as a random intercept to account for within-patient correlation between bilateral leads. Results Lead-tip positions showed significant interval displacement in the lateral, anterior, and caudal directions. In univariable mixed-effects analysis, intracranial air volume was significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.033, 95% CI 0.018-0.048, p < 0.001), whereas Angle A was not (β = -0.030, 95% CI - 0.067-0.007, p = 0.111). In a multivariable mixed-effects model including intracranial air volume and Angle A, intracranial air volume remained significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.0289, 95% CI 0.0110-0.0469, p = 0.002), while a larger Angle A was associated with less anterior displacement (β = -0.0270, 95% CI - 0.0535 to - 0.0004, p = 0.047). Conclusions Intracranial air volume was consistently associated with anterior STN-DBS lead-tip displacement between immediate and delayed postoperative CT. Intraoperative head position was also associated with anterior displacement after adjustment for intracranial air volume, although this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. These findings support efforts to minimize intracranial air entry during DBS implantation, while the potential influence of intraoperative head positioning requires further prospective investigation.

title: Multimodal MRI fusion and three-dimensional reconstruction for preoperative assessment of neurovascular compression in trigeminal neuralgia: A retrospective study.
abstract: Background Microvascular decompression is the primary surgical intervention for trigeminal neuralgia aimed at resolving neurovascular compression. Given the potential surgical risks, accurate preoperative assessment of neurovascular compression is critical. Although 3D visualization has been applied to preoperative assessment of neurovascular relationships, quantitative evaluation of the trigeminal nerve-vessel relationship and its association with intraoperative NVC findings remains limited. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed data from trigeminal neuralgia patients, hemifacial spasm controls and healthy controls. Preoperative 3D-FIESTA and 3D-TOF-MRA data were acquired and processed for 3D fusion reconstruction using 3D Slicer. After validating the model's reliability against intraoperative findings, trigeminal nerves were stratified into four subgroups. Anatomical morphological parameters and neurovascular relationships were quantitatively measured and compared among the subgroups. Immediate postoperative outcomes in trigeminal neuralgia patients were also evaluated. Results A total of 92 trigeminal neuralgia patients, 99 hemifacial spasm controls and 30 healthy controls were enrolled. The trigeminal neuralgia cohort was significantly older than the control group (63.1 vs. 54.3 years, P < 0.05). The preoperative 3D reconstruction demonstrated high consistency with intraoperative findings (accuracy: 93%, Kappa: 0.89). ROC analysis identified an optimal neurovascular distance threshold of 1.23 mm for predicting intraoperative neurovascular compression (AUC = 0.957). Morphological analysis showed no significant intergroup difference in nerve diameter (P = 0.458), whereas cisternal length differed significantly among the five groups (P < 0.001). The TNS group showed the shortest mean neurovascular distance (1.1 mm, P < 0.001) and the highest prevalence of neurovascular compression (NVC) (79.3%, P < 0.001). These findings remained consistent after inclusion of healthy controls. Immediate postoperative outcomes were not significantly associated with intraoperative NVC status or the 1.23-mm neurovascular distance. Conclusion This study confirmed the high diagnostic accuracy of preoperative 3D MRI fusion. Crucially, a neurovascular distance threshold of 1.23 mm was identified as an exploratory imaging marker for definite intraoperative compression. However, this threshold should not be regarded as an independent criterion for treatment selection.

title: Performance Analysis of Laplacian Re-Decomposition-Based PET-MRI Fusion for Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent critical stages along the continuum of cognitive decline. This study investigates the Laplacian Re-decomposition (LRD) method for fusing positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to develop a quantitative imaging biomarker for the classification of AD. Material and method Data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database were used in this study. T 1 , T 2 , T 2 -FLAIR, and T 2 *-weighted MRI sequences, together with [ 18 F]FDG-PET images, were preprocessed and fused using the LRD algorithm. Hippocampal and frontal lobe WM segmentation, performed via U-Net, enabled relative signal contrast (RSC) calculation as a quantitative biomarker for each modality and fused image. Fusion and segmentation performance were assessed using standard metrics. RSC statistically compared between diagnostic groups after adjustment for demographic confounds, and evaluated for classification performance using ROC/AUC analysis. Results The mean Dice coefficient achieved by the trained U-Net for hippocampus and frontal lobe WM segmentation were 0.93 and 0.95, respectively. ROC analysis revealed that the RSC extracted from T 1 -weighted images fused with PET outperformed other modalities for AD vs. Cognitively normal (CN) classification (AUC = 0.88, accuracy = 0.90). Also, T 2 -weighted images fused with PET, using RSC as a quantitative biomarker, achieved the best classification performance for AD vs. MCI (AUC = 0.81, accuracy = 0.81) and MCI vs. CN (AUC = 0.84, accuracy = 0.88) classification. Conclusion Our findings indicate that RSC extracted from LRD-fused images achieves competitive classification performance, supporting its potential as a quantitative biomarker for AD.

title: Diagnosis of Suspected Pituitary Microadenomas: The Complementary Role of Habitat-based Non-enhanced MRI Radiomics Features.
abstract: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). Radiomics features were extracted from both the entire pituitary gland and its habitat subregions, generated via unsupervised K-means clustering. Eight predictive models were constructed using logistic regression: a clinical model, an intra-pituitary radiomics model, three individual habitat models (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), an early-fusion model combining all habitats, an ensemble model integrating the probability outputs of the three habitat models, and a combined model that integrated clinical, intra-pituitary, and the optimal fusion model. title: TriKey AutoRefine: A Stability-Aware Framework Built on Pan-organ Segmentation Radiomics for Chronic Kidney Disease Staging.
abstract: Accurate and generalizable imaging‑based staging of chronic kidney disease remains challenging due to segmentation variability, feature instability, and heterogeneous clinical presentations. To address these gaps, a clinically aligned pan‑organ radiomics workflow for multi‑class chronic kidney disease staging was proposed. A total of 587 subjects from 3 centers were included, with chest and abdominal computed tomography scans paired with clinical and body-composition measurements. Segmentation‑induced variability was quantified within the pan‑organ segmentation system, revealing systematic anatomical and feature‑level patterns that enabled the construction of a robust and generalizable feature foundation. Building on these observations, the TriKey autorefine framework was introduced as a structured refinement strategy incorporating Shapley additive explanations guided refinement, clinically informed class weighting, and automatic parameter optimization. Using this framework, strong performance was achieved across chronic kidney disease staging tasks. In the standard 5‑class setting, high discriminative ability was obtained: training macro area under the curve 0.925 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.923-0.927); validation macro area under the curve 0.875 ± 0.0087 (95% CI 0.858-0.892). In the clinically actionable 4‑class grouping, even stronger performance was observed, with a mean macro area under the curve of 0.915 ± 0.0060 (95% CI 0.903-0.927). Interpretability was further supported through radiomics-clinical correlation analyses, which confirmed that the selected pan organ features correspond to measurable physiological variations associated with chronic kidney disease progression. This study demonstrates a robust, interpretable, and clinically grounded pan‑organ radiomics pipeline for chronic kidney disease staging, providing a generalizable foundation for future pan-organ radiomics research in nephrology and broader clinical imaging applications.

title: Locate Then Classify: A Heterogeneous Dual-Teacher Consensus Framework for Semi-Supervised Mammogram Diagnosis.
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a pathway to reduce the high cost of pixel-wise annotation in mammography, but classical teacher-student methods suffer from confirmation bias under extreme label scarcity. To address this, we propose a heterogeneous dual-teacher consensus framework (DTSL). Two complementary teachers, one detail-oriented (shallow SE attention) and one semantic-oriented (deep gated modulation), retain pseudo-labels only when they agree, thereby filtering unreliable predictions. Using only 30% of pixel-level labels, DTSL recovers 81.5% of fully supervised segmentation performance (Dice Similarity Coefficient, DSC = 0.626) and achieves a calcification intersection over union (IoU) of 0.700, reducing annotation cost by 70%. It outperforms standard Mean Teacher (78.1%) and nnU-Net plus Mean Teacher (79.8%). The trained segmentation encoder is then transferred to a classification head, injecting morphological priors into malignancy diagnosis. On the INbreast dataset, our classifier attains an AUC of 0.872 and a sensitivity of 0.837, surpassing the average sensitivity of four senior radiologists (0.803) by 3.4 percentage points (p < 0.05). Our model's superior sensitivity suggests its potential as a decision-support tool to reduce false negatives in screening, warranting prospective clinical validation. Grad-CAM visualizations confirm that attention maps align with radiologists' diagnostic cues. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/BrXNetCls-0C14/ .
