title: Building and Validating a Data-Governance Workflow for Artificial Intelligence-Based Tuberculosis Detection from Chest Radiographs, and Quantifying the Impact of Data Leakage.
abstract: Studies applying artificial intelligence (AI) to tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest radiographs (CXR) focus on models and metrics, yet the quality, provenance and reproducibility of the data workflow decide the reliability of results; duplicate images and non-patient-level splitting inflate evaluation metrics. We propose a seven-step data-governance workflow: multi-source standardisation, provenance management, three-hash deduplication (MD5, pHash, dHash), patient-level splitting, invariant-check auditing, lung segmentation and version freezing by data fingerprint. Four leakage scenarios (deduplication on or off; patient-level or random split) were repeated 20 times with paired splits and compared with the clean scenario on per-repeat differences. On 46,410 CXR images from seven public sources, the workflow removed duplicates at file and content level, standardised 16,554 TB Portals DICOM images, generated 34,554 lung masks without failure and sealed every layer with SHA-256 hashes. On the three-class multi-source corpus, the area under the curve (AUC) saturated near 0.997 in every scenario, consistent with source-class confounding; paired leakage effects were statistically detectable but below 0.1 percentage points. On a single-source probe task (drug resistance within TB Portals), random image-level splitting inflated the internal AUC by 1.7 percentage points (95% confidence interval 0.9 to 2.4; p = 0.001), or 1.2 points after a deduplication gap found during revision was repaired; in a holdout design, an internal gap of 1.1 points shrank to 0.4 points on a patient-disjoint holdout. The magnitude of leakage depends on data structure and must be measured; a rigorous governance workflow makes that measurement, and data reuse, verifiable.

title: Impact of Field Strength and Contrast Agents on Cardiac MRI Radiomic Features of the Myocardium and Blood Pool.
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of gadolinium-based contrast agents on cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. With Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval, eight healthy volunteers (38.5 ± 15.4 years; 4 males) underwent four consecutive cardiac MRI examinations using a Modified Look-Locker Inversion Recovery (MOLLI) sequence at 1.5T and 3T, with and without two contrast agents, gadopentetate dimeglumine (Gd-DTPA), and gadofosveset trisodium. Radiomic features were extracted from the myocardium and blood pool at the mid-ventricular level of the left ventricle using the first raw MOLLI image, corresponding to the shortest inversion time. Before contrast administration, switching from 1.5 to 3 T resulted in significant changes in 52% of myocardial and 56% of blood pool radiomic features. Contrast administration further altered radiomic feature values. At 1.5T, Gd-DTPA altered 42% of myocardial and 63% of blood pool features, whereas gadofosveset altered 73% and 85%, respectively. Similar patterns were observed at 3 T, with gadofosveset producing a greater proportion of altered features than Gd-DTPA (p < 0.05). Blood pool features were generally more sensitive to contrast administration than myocardial features. At 10 min after contrast administration, significant differences between the two contrast agents were observed in 48% of myocardial and 23% of blood pool features at 1.5T and in 72% and 60%, respectively, at 3 T. In conclusion, the administration and type of gadolinium-based contrast agents significantly alter cardiac MRI radiomic features across different magnetic field strengths. Future research should prioritize normalization strategies and evaluate feature robustness across larger patient populations to enhance the generalizability of cardiac radiomics.

title: Computer-Aided Diagnosis of Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer in Transrectal Ultrasound.
abstract: Diagnosing clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) using transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) remains a challenging task due to limited image contrast and the subtle appearance of malignant lesions. In this study, we propose a novel hybrid framework that integrates multi-modality and multi-task learning for csPCa classification from TRUS data. The framework leverages complementary information from B-mode and strain elastography (SE) imaging via a dual-stream encoder, enhanced by cross-modal attention gate (CMAG) modules at each level. These CMAG modules first adaptively integrate cross-modal features and then employ a gating mechanism to regulate the flow of cross-modal context into each modality-specific stream. To mitigate the scarcity of segmentation annotations, we introduce a multi-scale prototype-guided learning (MSPL) strategy, which propagates supervision signals from a small set of labeled samples to unlabeled ones by leveraging learned prototypes across multiple feature scales. This design allows the task-shared encoder to benefit from structural cues captured by the segmentation branch, even with minimal voxel-level supervision. Additionally, a context-aware multi-scale classifier (CMSC) aggregates hierarchical decoder features to further exploit the synergy between classification and segmentation tasks. The proposed method is evaluated on an in-house dataset containing 612 subjects who underwent prostate biopsy and attains favorable performance in identifying csPCa with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86. Extensive comparative and ablation results further highlight the efficacy of incorporating cross-modal interaction, prototype-guided learning, and context-aware classification for accurate and annotation-efficient csPCa diagnosis. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/mock1ngbrd/ProstateMMTNet .

title: SVF-net: A Dual-encoder Network with Adaptive Gated Fusion for Colorectal Polyp Segmentation.
abstract: Automatic colorectal polyp segmentation in retrospective still colonoscopy images remains challenging for small, low-contrast, partially occluded, or irregular lesions. We propose SVF-Net, a heterogeneous dual-encoder network combining a frozen SAM2 Hiera-L image trunk with a trainable MaxViT-RMLP-Small specialist branch. At four feature scales, the two streams are projected to a common width, spatially aligned, and reconciled by complementary channel-spatial gating before progressive decoding. Across five public benchmarks, three-run mean mDice is 0.922 on CVC-ClinicDB, 0.898 on Kvasir-SEG, 0.805 on CVC-ColonDB, 0.770 on ETIS-LaribPolypDB, and 0.896 on CVC-300. Matched projected-concatenation and fixed-weight ( G=0.5 ) controls retain the surrounding fusion path while removing input-dependent weighting; across ten matched training runs, adaptive gating gives higher mean mDice than both controls on all five datasets. Dataset-wide gate diagnostics on all 380 CVC-ColonDB and 196 ETIS cases indicate non-collapsed, scale- and region-dependent activations, while targeted one-factor sensitivity checks cover the MaxViT learning-rate multiplier, gate initialization, and auxiliary-loss weight. Matched per-case analyses further show that cross-domain gains are heterogeneous across lesion size, brightness, and an image-derived specular-reflection proxy. SVF-Net requires 92.8 ms per image (10.8 FPS) and 8.5 GB peak GPU memory on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 under the reported profiling protocol. The study evaluates retrospective static images only and does not establish real-time colonoscopy performance, prospective clinical effectiveness, or clinician benefit.

title: PW-GAN: Pseudo-Warping Field Guided GAN for Unsupervised Denoising of Fetal Brain MRI Images.
abstract: Fetal brain MRI commonly uses thick-slice acquisitions to mitigate motion artifacts and preserve in-plane image quality. Multiple motion-corrupted stacks of 2D slices can be retrospectively reconstructed into isotropic 3D volumes; however, volumes reconstructed from thicker slices generally exhibit lower image quality than those reconstructed from thinner slices because limited through-plane information results in residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. Existing post-reconstruction denoising methods are limited by their dependence on large-scale datasets comprising noisy-clean image pairs or insufficient modeling of inter-slice structural consistency. In this work, we propose a Pseudo-Warping Field Guided Unsupervised Generative Adversarial Network (PW-GAN), which formulates post-reconstruction denoising as unpaired translation between low- and high-quality MRI domains. By incorporating a pseudo-warping field module, our method significantly enhances inter-slice continuity in the reconstructed volumes while effectively suppressing residual noise and inter-slice structural discontinuities. On simulated data, PW-GAN achieved a PSNR of 39.65 dB and an SSIM of 0.9932. On real clinical data, it reduced the inter-slice warping error by up to 40% compared with unsupervised baselines. These results demonstrate that PW-GAN outperforms existing unsupervised models and achieves performance comparable to several state-of-the-art supervised methods. Qualitatively, PW-GAN produced cleaner results with smoother inter-slice structural transitions while preserving anatomical structures, demonstrating its effectiveness in post-reconstruction denoising of fetal brain MRI acquired from thick-slice scans.

title: Performance of Naïve Spectral Geometric Models in Histopathology AI.
abstract: Spectral geometric methods provide mathematically interpretable representations of tissue morphology, yet their standalone performance in histopathology artificial intelligence has not been systematically evaluated. This study benchmarks purely spectral pipelines across representative digital pathology and spatial omics tasks relative to convolutional baselines. Spectral features derived from graph Laplacians, heat kernel signatures, spectral wavelet energy, Slepian concentrations, fractal descriptors, and persistent homology were extracted from histopathology patches using fixed-grid graphs. Features were processed using spectral neural operators and gradient boosting. Four tasks were evaluated: binary breast cancer classification (BreaKHis), multi-class glioblastoma region-patch classification, spatial transcriptomics prediction (10× Visium), and spot-wise denoising. Cross-validation and leave-one-slide-out strategies were applied. Metrics included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean squared error, and Pearson correlation. Equivalence between spectral and CNN models was not established within the prespecified ±0.03 AUC margin. Purely spectral models achieved lower performance than convolutional baselines, with AUC differences of 0.12-0.23. The CNN→LGBM model achieved an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.06, balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.10, and AUC of 0.80 ± 0.13. Equivalence was not established within the prespecified margin. Fusion achieved balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.08, equal to the CNN baseline mean balanced accuracy, without surpassing CNN AUC. Spatial transcriptomics prediction showed limited cross-slide generalization (Pearson correlation 0.06), whereas spot-wise denoising under sparse conditions showed competitive performance. Spectral geometric models do not outperform convolutional methods for classification or segmentation but provide complementary utility in denoising and sparse spatial settings.

title: Field-Strength Dependence of Automated Subcortical Volumetry: A Paired 3 T-7 T Benchmarking Study of BrainSuite, FastSurfer and NextBrain.
abstract: Automated segmentation pipelines are widely used for quantitative assessment of subcortical brain structures, yet it remains unclear whether measurements obtained at different magnetic field strengths are numerically interchangeable. This study evaluated the cross-field agreement and inter-software consistency of automated subcortical volumetry using paired 3T and 7T structural MRI data from 30 healthy adults. T1-weighted images were independently processed using BrainSuite, FastSurfer and NextBrain. Volumes of the bilateral putamen, globus pallidus, nucleus accumbens, thalamus and caudate nucleus were analysed. Within-software agreement between 3 and 7T measurements was assessed using two-way mixed-effects, single-measure intraclass correlation coefficients for absolute agreement. Inter-software agreement was examined separately at 3T and 7T using both absolute agreement and consistency intraclass correlation coefficients. All within-software regional comparisons and selected inter-software comparisons were further evaluated using Bland-Altman analyses. Cross-field agreement varied markedly across software packages and anatomical regions. BrainSuite showed poor absolute agreement across all regions, whereas FastSurfer and NextBrain demonstrated moderate-to-good agreement in selected structures. Inter-software consistency was generally higher than absolute agreement, indicating preservation of relative participant ranking despite systematic differences in measured volumes. Segmentation failures were more frequent at 7T, particularly for BrainSuite. Bland-Altman analyses confirmed software- and region-specific systematic differences and wide limits of agreement. These findings indicate that the evaluated automated segmentation pipelines do not provide field-strength-invariant subcortical volume estimates. Measurements obtained at 3T and 7T, or using different software packages, should not be considered directly interchangeable without pipeline-specific validation or harmonisation.

title: Application and Improvement of YOLO11 for Carotid Plaque Detection in Handheld Ultrasound Images.
abstract: Early and accurate detection of carotid plaques is clinically significant for stroke risk assessment and primary care screening. To address challenges such as low resolution, small target size, and blurred boundaries in handheld ultrasound images of carotid plaques, this paper proposes an improved YOLO11n model named YOLO11-MGD. The model introduces the C2PSA_Mona module to suppress interference from normal anatomical structures and incorporates the C3k2_GCConv module to enhance global context modeling capabilities, thereby alleviating semantic fragmentation caused by heterogeneous plaques. Additionally, it integrates a Dynamic Head to achieve joint dynamic attention allocation across scale, space, and task dimensions, and it designs the Inner_MPDIoU loss function to improve bounding box regression accuracy for irregular plaques. Experimental results show that on a self-constructed dataset containing 2078 carotid plaque images, YOLO11-MGD achieves a mean mAP50 of 93.16%, outperforming several mainstream object detection models. While maintaining its lightweight advantage, the proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy and robustness of carotid plaque detection in low-quality ultrasound images and demonstrates good application value for primary care stroke risk screening.

title: Federated Learning-Based Multi-Task Framework for Privacy-Preserving Diagnosis of Muscle Invasion in Bladder Cancer.
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is critical for effective treatment planning, yet remains challenging owing to the scarcity of large-scale multicenter datasets and stringent data privacy requirements. To address these issues, we propose a federated learning (FL)-based framework for privacy-preserving MIBC diagnosis. The framework enables multi-institutional collaboration by training local models on site-specific data and aggregating them into a global model through secure parameter exchange, without transferring raw data. Furthermore, we introduce a multi-task learning architecture that simultaneously performs tumor segmentation and invasion classification, supported by a split-attention convolutional module designed to improve feature discrimination. Experimental results on MRI datasets from four medical centers show that our proposed multi‑task federated learning framework yields an AUC of 0.844, outperforming both single‑center models and the single‑task federated baseline (AUC = 0.829), and exhibits robustness under heterogeneous data distributions. Ablation experiments showed that incorporating the split-attention convolutional module increased the AUC of the multi-task FL model from 0.818 to 0.844.

title: Cardiac Image Segmentation Under Respiratory Motion Artifacts Using Different Modified U-Net Models.
abstract: Precise segmentation of cardiac magnetic resonance images (CMR) is essential to quantitative measurements of the heart, yet it is often affected by respiratory motion misregistration's and this is particularly common in free-breathing patient environments. These artifacts reduce the quality of the image and present a big challenge to traditional deep learning models such as the baseline U-Net. This paper carries out a systematic evaluation of the capabilities of four alternate U-Net architectures, Attention U-Net, Dense U-Net, Residual U-Net and Sharp U-Net, on CMR data with synthetically added motion artifacts of various intensities. To add synthetic artifacts, the deformation fields were employed that mimic the realistic breathing-induced deformations and obtained the clean, mild, moderate, and severe moving conditions. Hybrid loss function that combines Dice, Focal, and Tversky losses was used to train each model to create robustness to class imbalance and boundary degradation. The segmentation quality was assessed by the following evaluation metrics: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD) and Jaccard Index (JI). Their results show that Sharp U-Net had the best overall performance with the highest average DSC (0.927) and lowest HD (3.62 mm) in severe motion conditions. The region centered attention mechanisms were also capable of withstanding these in Attention U-Net. The dense and Residual U-Nets did not perform much better than the baseline, and did not perform as well when there were severe artifacts. These results show the significance of architectural improvements and motion consciousness instruction strategies in guaranteeing the dependable segmentation. The article provides a scalable and reproducible methodology to assess the performance of motion-robust deep learning models for CMR and adaptable for use in other clinical diagnostic applications where respiratory gating is not available. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and computationally practical approach to motion-robust cardiac MRI segmentation. Sharp U-Net achieved the highest segmentation performance under severe respiratory motion, with a DSC of 0.784, compared with 0.778 for Attention U-Net, while requiring a slightly higher inference latency of approximately 28-30 ms per 256 × 256 slice and GPU memory consumption of approximately 1.8 GB. This modest computational overhead represents a trade-off between improved boundary preservation and computational efficiency and should be considered when deploying the model in resource-constrained clinical environments. Across the clean, mild, moderate, and severe respiratory motion conditions, Sharp U-Net achieved an average DSC of 0.927. Under the most challenging severe-motion condition, the DSC decreased to 0.784, while maintaining an ASSD of 1.69 mm, sensitivity of 0.823, precision of 0.774, and RVE of 8.9%.

title: 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN: Pulmonary Nodule Detection Through Cross-Slice Feature Fusion and Dynamic Displacement Modeling.
abstract: Accurate pulmonary nodule detection in computed tomography (CT) remains challenging because small- and low-contrast nodules may resemble vessels and other anatomical structures on individual axial slices. We propose 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN, a multi-slice detection framework that incorporates structured local axial context into a two-stage detector. The five-slice interactive blending (5-SIB) strategy organizes five consecutive CT slices as an ordered contextual group and preserves slice-specific feature streams extracted by a shared two-dimensional backbone. The cross-slice feature fusion (CSFF) module applies slice-wise spatial self-attention at shallow feature levels and learnable cross-slice aggregation at deep feature and region-of-interest levels. The dynamic displacement constraint (DDC) models proposal displacement across adjacent slices using a positive-sample regression loss and a margin-based negative-sample contrastive loss, while a class-weighted focal loss alleviates foreground-background imbalance. The model was evaluated on a private hospital dataset, LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb using patient-level data partitions. On the private hospital dataset, 3D-DDN achieved an average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5 (AP 0.5 ) of 75.80% ± 1.05%, a sensitivity of 89.33% ± 1.91%, and a competition performance metric (CPM) of 91.20% ± 1.50%. The corresponding AP 0.5 values on LIDC-IDRI and LNDb were 66.27% ± 0.45% and 48.20% ± 0.30%, respectively. Ablation experiments showed that direct five-slice stacking degraded performance, whereas structured feature fusion and displacement supervision recovered the performance loss and improved the overall detection profile. These results indicate that ordered cross-slice representation, hierarchical feature fusion, and proposal-displacement supervision provide complementary mechanisms for incorporating local three-dimensional context.

title: M4DTrack: A DICOM-Based Imaging Informatics Workflow for User-Supervised 4DCT Lung Tumor Motion Reporting.
abstract: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is routinely used in radiotherapy simulation to evaluate respiration-induced tumor motion, but the motion information is often reviewed visually rather than captured as structured, phase-resolved data. We developed and evaluated M4DTrack, a DICOM-based imaging-informatics workflow for user-supervised 4DCT lung tumor motion analysis and structured, exportable three-dimensional center-of-mass (CoM) motion reporting. M4DTrack imports phase-resolved DICOM CT images, groups images by respiratory phase, displays linked axial/coronal/sagittal views, supports crosshair-based tumor localization and HU inspection, and applies seed or linked 3D-box initialization with sequential phase-to-phase HU-volume propagation. An 8-case lower-lobe lung 4DCT dataset (80 respiratory phases) was analyzed. Directional amplitudes, 3D vector amplitude, maximum phase-wise displacement, and agreement with independent ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were quantified. HU-weighted CoM amplitudes were 2.44 ± 1.44 mm, 2.64 ± 1.37 mm, and 6.04 ± 2.48 mm in X, Y, and Z patient-coordinate directions, respectively. Mean 3D vector amplitude was 7.26 ± 2.50 mm, and mean maximum phase-wise 3D displacement was 6.20 ± 2.10 mm. Biases versus ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were 0.01, - 0.84, and 0.23 mm for X, Y, and Z, respectively, with a 3D vector amplitude bias of - 0.29 mm. M4DTrack provides a user-supervised imaging-informatics bridge between qualitative 4DCT cine review and structured quantitative motion documentation. The pilot results support feasibility for generating exportable, phase-resolved tumor-motion metrics while preserving user-supervised review of 4DCT artifacts, HU-capture uncertainty, adjacent anatomy, and differences between CoM-based and extent-based measurements.

title: Radiomic Signatures of Smoking in Visually Normal Lung Parenchyma: Bilateral CT Analysis Using Machine Learning.
abstract: Smoking is associated with structural and functional alterations in the lungs, some of which may be reflected in quantitative imaging features. Radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional image-derived descriptors and may provide information beyond routinely available clinical variables. We investigated whether bilateral lung radiomics, both independently and integrated with clinical variables, could classify patient-level smoking status. An exploratory secondary analysis was also performed to assess whether radiomic and clinical feature representations could discriminate smoking exposure intensity among smokers. A total of 506 patients were included, comprising 253 smokers and 253 nonsmokers. Right and left lung radiomic features were extracted separately from visually normal-appearing lung parenchyma on thoracic CT images. Multiple feature representations were evaluated, including right lung radiomics, left lung radiomics, concatenated right-left radiomics, summary/asymmetry radiomics, clinical variables alone, and radiomics combined with clinical variables. Clinical variables included age, sex, height, weight, and body mass index. Pack-years were excluded from the binary smoking status classification models to avoid target-related information leakage. For each binary classification task, a balanced internal hold-out set containing 25 smokers and 25 nonsmokers was reserved, while the remaining patients were evaluated using stratified tenfold cross-validation. Four feature selection or dimensionality reduction strategies and five classifier families were assessed, resulting in 435 model configurations across the main cohort and sex-specific subgroup analyses. Threshold selection was performed using the Youden index derived from cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. For the exploratory smoking exposure analysis, 253 smokers with available pack-year information were categorized into < 10, 10-20, and > 20 pack-year groups and evaluated using pooled stratified tenfold cross-validation. The best-performing radiomics-based configurations showed higher discrimination than the clinical-only configuration. The clinical-only random forest model achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.673 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.610. Among radiomics-only configurations, concatenated bilateral radiomics achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.734 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.712. The strongest hold-out discrimination was obtained using concatenated bilateral radiomics combined with clinical variables, ReliefF feature selection, and stacking classification, achieving a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.803, balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.720, and specificity of 0.680. Feature selection stability analysis showed that the final concatenated bilateral radiomics + clinical configuration retained five clinical variables and 15 radiomic features, several of which were repeatedly selected across cross-validation folds. Sex-specific subgroup analyses showed moderate but variable performance. In the exploratory three-class smoking exposure analysis, integrating left lung radiomics with clinical variables yielded the most balanced class-wise performance, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (0.658) and the highest sensitivity for the intermediate 10-20 pack-year group (0.417), although the clinical-only model achieved the highest macro-AUC. Bilateral lung radiomics showed potential for patient-level smoking status classification, particularly when combined with clinical variables. These findings suggest that quantitative imaging features could provide complementary information beyond routinely available patient-level variables. The exploratory smoking exposure analysis further suggested that radiomics + clinical configurations may contain limited information related to smoking exposure intensity, although intermediate exposure remained challenging to discriminate. However, the moderate performance, subgroup variability, and lack of external validation indicate that this approach should be considered investigational until confirmed in larger independent cohorts.

title: Impact of different pre-processing methods combined with combat harmonization on the reproducibility of radiomics features in healthy human brain MRI.
abstract: Objective To explore the effect of different pre-processing methods combined with ComBat harmonization on improving the stability of MRI radiomic features in healthy human brains. Methods T1FLAIR and T2W scans from 416 healthy subjects across four MRI systems underwent seven pipelines (Original, N4, Z-Score, DTN, Nyul, WhiteStripe, RAVEL). SynthSeg segmented white/gray matter for 93 IBSI radiomic features. Stability was quantified via covariate-adjusted standardized scanner effect (d = β_scanner/σ_res, |d|< 0.2) with 95% bootstrap CIs, supplemented by PCA and LOOCV AUC. Friedman and post-hoc McNemar tests with Bonferroni correction compared pipelines. FDR-corrected partial correlations assessed retention of significant age and sex associations after ComBat. Results Raw data exhibited extremely low stability with substantial scanner-induced effects, while scanner classification AUC was close to 1.0. ComBat harmonization significantly improved stability across all pipelines and reduced AUC to near 0.5. Within this dataset, DTN_ComBat demonstrated consistently high stability; pairwise statistical comparisons indicated it showed more favourable stability performance relative to most other pipelines for the majority of tested contrasts, with stable proportions exceeding 90% across all sequences and tissues, and retained 75.0-100.0% of statistically significant age and sex-related associations. Conclusion Unprocessed brain MRI radiomic features exhibit poor cross‑scanner stability. Within this dataset, ComBat effectively reduces scanner‑related feature‑distribution differences, while preserving most statistically‑significant age and sex‑related associations. Among tested pre-processing pipelines, DTN_ComBat showed comparatively favourable performance under the present healthy‑brain MRI scanner‑protocol configurations.

title: Evaluating Image Quality of Cone Beam Computed Tomography Using HyperSight® on the Varian TrueBeam.
abstract: Purpose The study evaluated the image quality of the cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) system on Varian TrueBeam linear accelerators with HyperSight (TB-HS) and compared it with the standard TrueBeam system (TB-S). Particular emphasis was placed on changes relevant to offline adaptive radiotherapy (ART). Methods Image quality was assessed using a Catphan 504 phantom on two TB-HS and two TB-S machines. Quantitative parameters included HU accuracy, uniformity, contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), modulation transfer function (MTF), low-contrast visibility (LCV), and noise power spectrum (NPS). Measurements were performed at 100 kV and 125 kV using default clinical CBCT protocols and reconstruction algorithms. Planning CT images acquired with matching clinical protocols served as reference values. Statistical comparisons of image quality parameters between techniques and agreement with internationally recommended tolerance criteria were performed using the pairwise linear mixed models and McNemar's tests, respectively. Additionally, eight radiographers conducted a blinded subjective image quality evaluation of CBCT images from 15 patients before and after the HyperSight installation RESULTS: Catphan analysis showed that TB-HS improved HU accuracy for high-density inserts, while uniformity and CNR showed minor, mostly non-significant differences. Spatial resolution, noise characteristics, and LCV remained unchanged. Both techniques generally met the tolerance criteria, though TB-HS did so more consistently. Subjective image quality evaluation showed no overall preference. Conclusion The HyperSight upgrade provided minor image quality enhancements but demonstrated no clear clinical advantage. Nevertheless, findings support the potential of HyperSight for offline ART. However, further investigations in patient-based applications are needed to confirm its clinical value.

title: Abdominal Ultrasound Simulation from Semantic Labels Using Paired Label-to-Physics-Based Image Translation.
abstract: Purpose Current abdominal ultrasound (US) simulation methods often require CT-based anatomical references for ray-casting, limiting deformation, and pathology variability. We propose a learning-based pipeline trained to predict physics-based images derived from CT scans from semantic labels, enabling controlled simulations without patient-specific CT volumes at inference time. Methods We introduce a two-stage pipeline that maps anatomical segmentations to realistic US images through a simplified US image. Stage I synthesizes this image from semantic labels using models trained on CT-based ray-casting outputs. Stage II refines it into a realistic US scan using anatomically guided unpaired translation. Deformations and pathologies are generated by editing anatomical maps. Results We evaluated Pix2Pix and the Semantic Diffusion Model (SDM) in Stage I, followed by segmentation-guided CycleGAN (SG-CycleGAN) refinement in Stage II. SDM significantly outperformed Pix2Pix in morphological metrics, including MAE ↓ (19.85 vs. 21.65), SSIM ↑ (0.28 vs. 0.24), and mIoU ↑ (0.43 vs. 0.29), whereas Pix2Pix yielded better perceptual point estimates (LPIPS ↓ : 0.17 vs. 0.19; FID ↓ : 0.32 vs. 0.37; KID ↓ : 0.25 vs. 0.48). Conclusion Training paired generative models with physics-based supervision enables approximation of CT-derived ray-casting outputs at inference time directly from semantic labels. Although the pipeline does not require patient-specific CT volumes at inference time, CT-derived segmentations and ray-casting simulations remain necessary to train Stage I. Once trained, the framework enables controllable healthy and pathological simulations through semantic map modification.

title: Automated 3D Analysis of Hip Morphology in a Young Adult Population.
abstract: Purpose Although many factors contribute to the development of hip OA, structural findings, such as acetabular dysplasia, are recognized as strong contributing factors to early degenerative changes. However, conventional two-dimensional imaging cannot fully capture the joint's three-dimensional anatomy. This study aimed to develop and validate an automated MRI-based method for 3D hip morphology analysis. Methods MRI data from 2,454 participants in the Generation R Cohort (1,199 males; 1,255 females; mean age 18.4 years; mean BMI 22.7 kg/m 2 ) were analyzed. An nnU-Net deep learning model, trained on 40 manually segmented hips, automatically segmented femoral bone, acetabular bone, and femoral and acetabular cartilage. Model performance was assessed using Dice scores. From the segmentations, five categories of morphological features were computed: basic geometric metrics, cartilage volumes, angular measurements, coverage metrics, and joint space width. Sex differences were evaluated using independent t-tests, and BMI-related differences using one-way ANOVA. Results The model achieved Dice scores of 0.97 for femoral bone, 0.90 for acetabular bone, 0.76 for femoral cartilage, and 0.77 for acetabular cartilage. Reference ranges were established for all biomarkers. Significant differences were observed between males and females and across BMI groups. Conclusion Automated 3D hip morphology analysis using MRI is feasible and reliable. The generated reference values enhance understanding of hip development and anatomical variation in young adults and support future large-scale, reproducible assessments. All developed code is made openly available at https://gitlab.com/radiology/msk/genr/hip/hip-segmentation-and-biomarkers.

title: Age-associated radiomic phenotyping in mice using multi-energy photon-counting and preclinical CT: an exploratory study.
abstract: To investigate whether CT-derived radiomic features capture imaging patterns associated with chronological age groups in mice and to assess the influence of imaging platform and photon-counting CT reconstruction strategy on classification performance. Female C57BL/6NRj mice from three chronological age groups (28, 88, and 99 weeks; n = 11) underwent clinical photon-counting CT (PCCT) and preclinical Albira II CT. Heart, liver, and spleen were segmented and radiomic features were extracted. The individual mouse was defined as the independent biological unit. Model development and evaluation used nested leave-one-mouse-out cross-validation with all preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and, where applicable, reconstruction-energy selection restricted to the respective training folds. Organ-level class probabilities were averaged to generate one mouse-level prediction. Monoenergetic PCCT reconstructions from 40 to 180 keV were evaluated, including a fully nested energy-and-pipeline selection analysis. A grouped mouse-level permutation analysis with 200 permutations was performed for the primary monoenergetic workflow. Albira II correctly classified 5/11 mice (45.5%; 95% CI, 21.3-72.0%), whereas PCCT-SPP correctly classified 10/11 mice (90.9%; 95% CI, 62.3-98.4%). The fully nested monoenergetic PCCT workflow correctly classified 9/11 mice (81.8%; 95% CI, 52.3-94.9%; balanced accuracy, 83.3%; macro-F1, 83.3%). Energy-specific performance varied considerably: 110 keV showed the highest accuracy (81.8%) and was selected in 7/11 outer folds, whereas the highest macro one-vs-rest AUC occurred at 130 keV (0.867). None of the 200 permuted analyses reached the observed fully nested monoenergetic accuracy (plus-one corrected Monte-Carlo p = 0.005). CT-derived radiomic features showed chronological age-group-associated patterns in this exploratory murine cohort, with classification performance varying substantially across imaging platforms and reconstruction strategies. PCCT-SPP showed the numerically highest performance, while monoenergetic PCCT demonstrated pronounced energy dependence without evidence for a universally optimal reconstruction energy. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts and correlation with independent biological-aging reference measures.

title: Interpreting ocular age estimates: source, output, evidence, and clinical meaning.
abstract: Ocular age estimates derived from fundus photographs, optical coherence tomography, ocular fluids, systemic omics, and multimodal models are increasingly reported in years. The eye is unusually tractable for organ-specific aging research because it is paired, repeatedly imageable, locally treatable, and linked to quantitative function. The familiar scale can obscure differences in what was measured, what the model was developed to predict, which quantity is reported, and what the study design can support. Existing frameworks classify visual-aging biomarkers by biological domain and context of use. We propose an eye-specific framework organized around five declarations: proximal source; development target; reported quantity; evidence design; and intended use. Laterality, reference population, disease and treatment context, technical version, and uncertainty in the stated output remain essential annotations. A raw age gap is a cross-sectional residual, and an age-adjusted deviation requires calibration outside the outcome-analysis sample. Repeated application of a cross-sectional model does not establish an individual aging rate; longitudinal claims require repeated measurements against a longitudinal reference and change distinguishable from measurement variability. Visual-aging claims also need psychophysical, performance-based, or patient-reported validation. Differences across measurement domains must be assessed both against measurement error and against the distribution expected in the reference population. A persistent difference may support a candidate biological pattern only after technical and clinical explanations have been evaluated. Prognostic and clinical claims require separate prospective and decision-level evidence. These distinctions prevent a cross-sectional age residual from being mistaken for an aging rate, a prognostic marker, or a clinically actionable test.

title: Artificial intelligence decision support for breast ultrasound: potential to reduce benign biopsies.
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to evaluate the potential impact of a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support tool for breast ultrasound in reducing benign biopsies. Methods This study was conducted at two academic medical centers from March to May 2025 following the clinical implementation of an FDA-cleared AI-based decision support tool for breast ultrasound interpretation (Koios DS; New York, NY). Fourteen breast imaging radiologists documented BI-RADS 4 (suspicious) cases, along with the corresponding AI output. AI assessments were compared with biopsy pathology results to characterize AI classification within this selected cohort. Results Overall, 271 lesions in 253 women (mean age, 54 years; range, 24-92 years) were categorized as BI-RADS 4 and were biopsied, aspirated, and/or surgically excised. Of these, 23.2% (63/271) yielded malignant pathology, while 76.8% (208/271) were benign. The AI tool classified 90.5% (57/63) of malignant lesions as BI-RADS 4 and 9.5% (6/63) as BI-RADS 2 or 3. Among benign cases, the AI tool assigned 41.8% (87/208) as BI-RADS 2 (benign), 18.8% (39/208) as BI-RADS 3 (probably benign), and 39.4% (82/208) as BI-RADS 4 (suspicious). Retrospective application of the AI output to biopsy triage decisions suggests the potential for reduction in benign biopsy recommendations, with 60.6% (126/208) of benign lesions classified by the AI tool as BI-RADS 2 or 3. Conclusion AI may help reduce benign biopsy recommendations among lesions assessed as BI-RADS 4 by radiologists; however, careful integration with radiologist judgment and clinical history is essential to ensure timely cancer diagnosis.

title: A breast clinical scoring system to identify women with Idiopathic granulomatous Mastitis.
abstract: Purpose Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis (IGM) is a benign inflammatory breast condition that can resemble mastitis or malignancy clinically and radiographically. We aimed to develop a quantitative scoring system, based off the Komen Inflammatory Breast Cancer (IBC) scoring system [1], evaluating clinical and radiologic features to distinguish IGM from benign and malignant breast conditions. Methods We conducted a retrospective chart review of biopsy-proven IGM patients diagnosed from 2014 to 2025 via institutional electronic medical records. Clinical symptom onset, features, and diagnostic imaging were analyzed. A continuous scoring scale (1-50) was created, encompassing three categories: symptom onset, clinical features, and radiographic findings. Scores of IGM patients were compared with those of patients diagnosed with IBC, mastitis (lactational and non-lactational), and locally advanced breast cancer (LABC). Welch's two-sample t-test assessed statistical differences, and Youden index identified the optimal score threshold for predicting IGM. Results Among 148 IGM patients, predominantly Hispanic (56.8%) and Asian (26.7%), the mean age was 37.2 years, older than mastitis patients and younger than IBC patients. Key clinical features included pain or painful breast mass (100%), fistula or draining wound (77.7%), erythema (94.6%), and phlegmon (87.8%). Imaging revealed mass with collection in 84.6% and multiple masses/collections in 38.9%. The mean IGM score (35.5) was significantly higher than scores for IBC, mastitis, and LABC groups (14.4, 18, and 15.2, respectively; p ≤ 0.05). A score ≥ 24.5 predicted IGM with 93% sensitivity and 95% specificity. Conclusions This novel scoring system provides an objective framework to differentiate IGM from similar breast conditions, facilitating early diagnosis and guiding appropriate management. Clinical trial number not applicable.

title: Awareness, need and utilization of breast cancer risk management resources in women with hereditary cancer susceptibility.
abstract: Background Germline genetic testing is increasing. While testing barriers are well characterized, less is known about post-testing needs and utilization of screening and prevention resources by women with pathogenic variants (PVs) in breast cancer susceptibility genes. Methods A 38-question online survey was developed by Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered (FORCE), a patient advocacy group, and administered electronically to subscribers from February-May 2024. Study eligibility criteria included female sex and a germline PV conferring elevated lifetime risk of breast cancer (ATM, BARD1, BRCA1, BRCA2, CDH1, CHEK2, PALB2, PTEN, RAD51C, RAD51D, STK11, or TP53). Results Of 1,025 respondents who initiated the survey, 937 were women. Most were non-Hispanic White (91.7%) and from the United States (81.6%). The most common PVs were BRCA2 (31.4%), BRCA1 (25.5%) and CHEK2 (9.2%). The most frequently used resources were education and information services about medical options (39.3%) and peer support (28.1%). Few respondents used financial navigation (4.0%) or financial support (5.3%), but up to 45% reported needing these services. Among breast screening users (53.8% used mammogram, 42.2% magnetic resonance imaging, 19.4% ultrasound), 37.8% found it hard to prepare emotionally for results and 14% found it hard to pay for screening. One-third (37.1%) of respondents found deciding whether to have risk-reducing mastectomy hard; two-thirds (64.0%) found physical recovery hard, more than half (60.2%) found emotional recovery hard, and one-quarter (24.7%) found paying for risk-reducing mastectomy hard. Conclusion In this contemporary sample of women at elevated risk of breast cancer, more than one-third had unmet financial needs and up to two-thirds had difficulty with screening or risk-reducing surgery. Closing these gaps will be essential to improve outcomes for women with hereditary breast cancer.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA and Acute Myocarditis: A Comparative Multiparametric Evaluation.
abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) and acute myocarditis (AM) often present with overlapping clinical features and biomarker profiles, making early differential diagnosis challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) is the reference modality for etiological assessment through functional evaluation and multiparametric tissue characterization. The aim of this study was to compare clinical and CMR characteristics of patients with MINOCA and suspected AM, and to identify imaging features enabling accurate differentiation. We retrospectively analyzed 127 consecutive patients undergoing CMR (February 2021-October 2024): 62 with suspected MINOCA and 65 with suspected AM. Clinical data, laboratory findings, ECG, and CMR parameters (cine imaging, T1/T2 mapping, extracellular volume [ECV], and late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) were assessed. MINOCA patients were older (median 59 years) and predominantly female (64.5%), whereas AM patients were younger (median 29 years) and mainly male (81.5%). AM was associated with higher troponin and inflammatory markers. title: The predictive value of <sup>99m</sup>Tc-MIBI SPECT/<sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging in patients with unrevascularized coronary chronic total occlusion and left ventricular dysfunction.
abstract: To explore the predictive value of hibernating myocardium detected by single photon emission computed tomography (SEPCT)/positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging for the adverse cardiovascular events in unrevascularized chronic coronary total occlusion (CTO) patients with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction. Additionally, we explore whether hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory can independently predictive outcomes. Patients with at least one unrevascularized CTO on coronary angiography and LV dysfunction and who underwent rest 99m Tc-MIBI SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging as well as 18 F-FDG PET myocardial metabolic imaging were enrolled. All patients were followed up through telephone interviews and review of medical records. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, the extents of hibernating myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories, the extent of total scarred myocardium, and the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were calculated according to the segmental perfusion/metabolism score and the segmental assignment of coronary dominance and the results of coronary angiography. The Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to analyze the relationship between the extent of hibernating or scarred myocardium and adverse cardiovascular events. Seventy eight patients were included in the final analysis. The median follow-up duration was 70.2 (27.7, 80.3) months. The extent of total hibernating myocardium and the extent of hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory were both independent predictors for cardiac death [hazards ratio (HR) = 1.289, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.083-1.533, P = 0.004; HR = 1.262, 95% CI 1.022-1.557, P = 0.030] and the composite endpoint events (HR = 1.190, 95% CI 1.032-1.372, P = 0.016; HR = 1.273, 95% CI 1.025-1.581, P = 0.029). The extent of hibernating myocardium in the non-CTO territory, the extent of total scarred myocardium, the extents of scarred myocardium in the CTO and non-CTO territories were all not associated with the outcome. 99m Tc-MIBI / 18 F-FDG SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion/metabolic imaging has an important predictive value for prognosis in unrevascularized CTO patients with LV dysfunction. The extent of total hibernating myocardium, especially hibernating myocardium in the CTO territory, was an independent predictor for adverse cardiovascular events.

title: Amyloid-targeted PET after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy for cardiac amyloidosis: a systematic review.
abstract: To assess myocardial positron emission tomography (PET) positivity after negative or low-grade bone scintigraphy, while distinguishing test discordance from independently confirmed cardiac amyloidosis. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched through 5 August 2026, with targeted source assessment through 2 October 2026. Negative and low-grade imaging denoted Perugini grades 0 and 1, respectively; study-defined negative results were described separately. Eligibility required linked PET and bone-scan results with an extractable denominator. Acquisition modality, PET thresholds and cardiac reference standards were examined. A restricted synthesis required documented tomographic acquisition; a broader three-report synthesis was exploratory. Nine reports provided extractable paired results. In the hereditary transthyretin subgroup examined with carbon-11 Pittsburgh compound B, 20/23 participants were PET-positive after excluding one acquired, domino-transplant case. The exploratory pooled proportion was 87.0% (95% profile-likelihood confidence interval, 68.5-97.8%). Restriction to clearly documented cohort-wide tomography retained only two reports, precluding the planned pooled analysis. Uptake definitions and cardiac verification differed substantially. General diagnostic studies without complete bone-grade denominators, including REVEAL, were excluded from the eligible synthesis and retained as context. PET positivity is common in selected hereditary transthyretin cohorts with negative or low-grade bone scans, but does not establish cardiac amyloidosis or earlier diagnosis. Conditional diagnostic accuracy remains unresolved. Prospective paired studies require tomographic localization, tracer-specific thresholds and independent cardiac verification.

title: THINKERS-X: multisequence MRI radiomics in a mixture-of-experts model for outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation in lung cancer brain metastases treated with radiosurgery.
abstract: We developed THINKERS-X: Lung, the eXtended multimodal evolution of THINKERS-Lung, to determine whether multisequence MRI radiomics provides incremental value for lesion-specific outcome prediction and exploratory dose-scenario evaluation after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for lung cancer brain metastases. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 767 patients with 3,728 lung cancer brain metastases treated with GKRS. THINKERS-X preserved the original mixture-of-experts and discrete-time survival architecture while adding a dedicated computational neuroradiology expert. Approximately 2,400 radiomic features per metastasis were extracted from pretreatment FSPGR/T1-weighted postcontrast, T2-weighted, and SWAN MRI. Validation used patient-grouped 5-fold cross-validation and a completely closed patient-grouped internal holdout cohort. In grouped cross-validation, THINKERS-X achieved a mean AUC 12 of 0.919 ± 0.021 versus 0.876 for THINKERS-Lung (paired difference, 0.043; 95% CI 0.026-0.061; p < 0.001). In the internal holdout cohort, AUC 12 improved from 0.863 to 0.929 (95% CI 0.895-0.958), with a paired difference of 0.066 (95% CI 0.031-0.101; p < 0.001). Mean absolute error decreased from 1.26 to 0.84 months. The calibrated Brier score was 0.039, calibration slope 0.94, and intercept 0.04. Radiomics altered model-derived dose-response profiles in 30.0% of metastases and the model-ranked candidate dose in 23.9%. THINKERS-X improved lesion-specific longitudinal prediction, temporal accuracy, and probabilistic calibration beyond THINKERS-Lung while materially altering exploratory dose-scenario evaluation in a subset of metastases. External multicenter and prospective validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: Giant macular hole in a female patient with X-linked Alport syndrome harboring a novel de novo COL4A5 variant.
abstract: Purpose To report a female patient with genetically confirmed X-linked Alport syndrome (AS) presenting with progressive retinal thinning and giant macular hole formation. Methods A 28-year-old woman with a history of bilateral LASIK surgery was referred for evaluation of bilateral progressive maculopathy. Comprehensive ophthalmic examinations, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and full-field and multifocal electroretinography (ERG), were performed. Targeted next-generation sequencing of COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5 genes was performed. Results At presentation, decimal best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 0.7 in the right eye (OD) and 1.2 in the left eye (OS). The patient had no hearing loss or family history of renal or ocular disease. OCT revealed bilateral retinal thinning. During follow-up, progressive thinning of all retinal layers was observed, and a macular hole developed in OS, gradually enlarging from 546 µm at age 34 to a giant macular hole measuring 1684 µm in minimum diameter at age 39. At 37 years of age, full-field ERG demonstrated preserved rod system function with mild cone system dysfunction, and multifocal ERG showed significantly reduced macular responses bilaterally. Genetic testing identified a novel de novo heterozygous COL4A5 variant (p.Gly775Val), classified as pathogenic, confirming X-linked AS. Conclusions X-linked AS may present with progressive diffuse macular thinning and giant macular hole formation even in female patients without hearing loss or a family history. AS should be considered in the differential diagnosis of unexplained bilateral macular thinning and giant macular hole in women.

title: Psychological Support in Prenatal Diagnosis: The Parental Perspective.
abstract: The communication of a diagnosis of fetal malformation is a very complex event for the parental couple to experience. The aim of the study is to report a planned evaluation of an ongoing psychological support within a prenatal diagnosis clinic, examining the extent to which it represents a source of support service for parental couples. An ad hoc semi-structured questionnaire was administered to couples who had received a prenatal diagnosis of fetal malformation, regardless of whether they had received psychological support. Descriptive analyses were performed on quantitative items, while an inductive thematic analysis was applied to open-ended responses to identify recurring themes. The results show that the majority of couples who used the support reported being satisfied with it. The ultrasound examination and specialist consultation were considered by the majority of the participants to be the most appropriate moments to receive the counseling. On the other hand, 41.38% of the couples who did not receive support would have liked to have received it. Finally, the majority of the couples, regardless of whether they received psychological support, would recommend that couples in similar situations seek psychological support and that other hospital facilities integrate such services. The results show that among couples who have received psychological support, most reported having benefited from it. In the absence of the psychologist within the multidisciplinary team, however, only a few participants have actively requested it. The findings are discussed in terms of the clinical relevance of psychological support at the time of fetal diagnostic assessments and specialist consultation.

title: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation in prostate cancer detection: current evidence, clinical positioning, and translational gaps.
abstract: GSTP1 promoter hypermethylation is one of the most consistently documented molecular alterations in prostate cancer, with high prevalence in malignant tissue and a well-established relationship with transcriptional silencing. However, despite more than two decades of biological and diagnostic investigation, GSTP1-based testing has not acquired a clearly defined stand-alone role in contemporary prostate cancer detection. This narrative review examines why extensive biological evidence has not translated into routine clinical use and where, if anywhere, GSTP1 testing might provide meaningful value within current diagnostic pathways. Evidence from prostate tissue, urine and circulating cell-free DNA is considered alongside the effects of biospecimen selection, preanalytical handling, CpG target selection, assay design and interpretation thresholds. Tissue demonstrates the most reproducible signal and has achieved partial clinical translation through multiplex testing such as ConfirmMDx, whereas urinary and blood-based approaches remain investigational. Recent urinary findings, including in men with moderately elevated PSA, are promising but remain preliminary and have not established incremental value beyond contemporary risk assessment, biomarkers and multiparametric MRI. The translational priority is therefore not to demonstrate again that GSTP1 detects prostate cancer, but to determine whether a standardised assay provides reproducible, nonredundant and clinically actionable information at a defined decision point. Future development should prioritise clearly specified target populations, analytically validated assay configurations, clinically significant prostate cancer as the relevant endpoint, and prospective evaluation against contemporary diagnostic pathways.

title: Leveraging traditional and advanced machine learning for comprehensive oncology data integration and outcome prediction.
abstract: Background Outcome prediction in neuro-oncology remains challenging due to heterogeneity in tumor biology, imaging characteristics, treatment response, and patient-specific clinical factors. Although molecular databases have advanced understanding of brain tumor biology, many datasets lack broader data necessary for generalizable predictive modeling. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being explored to integrate these heterogeneous data sources and support precision neuro-oncology. Methods A narrative review was performed using PubMed and Embase to identify studies evaluating oncology databases, ML models, multimodal data integration, and AI applications relevant to neuro-oncology. Studies published between 2020 and 2026 were preferentially reviewed, with additional landmark studies included when relevant. Results Traditional ML approaches including regression-based models, random forests, support vector machines, and gradient boosting algorithms have been applied to survival prediction, recurrence classification, treatment response estimation, and molecular biomarker prediction using clinical, imaging, molecular, and population-level datasets. More advanced architectures including natural language processing, large language models, vision transformers, geometric deep learning, and graph neural networks have expanded the ability to analyze unstructured and multimodal data sources including radiology reports, histopathology slides, MRI volumes, molecular datasets, and electronic health records. Multimodal AI systems integrating imaging, molecular, histopathologic, clinical, and socioeconomic data frequently demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with single-modality models. However, widespread clinical implementation remains limited by dataset heterogeneity, limited external validation, interpretability concerns, and inconsistent representation across patient populations. Conclusions AI and ML approaches are increasingly capable of integrating complex neuro-oncology datasets in ways that more closely reflect real-world clinical decision-making. Although most current models remain investigational, multimodal AI frameworks may ultimately improve prognostic assessment, treatment stratification, and precision neuro-oncology care. Continued progress will require larger representative datasets, improved data harmonization, external validation, and clinically interpretable models.

title: Volumetric analysis of radiographic changes after stereotactic radiosurgery for treatment of non-responding brain metastases.
abstract: Purpose Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) effectively treats brain metastases, yet some lesions ultimately require post-SRS surgery due to local failure. We examined whether the use of volumetric changes in FLAIR hyperintensity and/or necrosis in conjunction with enhancing volumetric changes after Gamma Knife SRS correlate with pathological outcome at subsequent surgery. Methods We queried our institutional database for patients who received first-time SRS for a single brain metastasis and later underwent surgical resection of the same lesion. Tumor volumes were measured manually before SRS and at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months post-treatment. FLAIR:enhancing (FER) and enhancing:necrotic ratios were analyzed. Linear mixed-effects models assessed variables influencing volume trajectories; Pearson correlation examined associations with pathological outcome. Results Thirty-six patients met inclusion criteria. Mean enhancing volume changed - 28.5%, - 25.8%, and - 18.9% from baseline at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months, respectively. Mean FLAIR volume changed - 16.9%, - 22.2%, and - 2.4% at the same intervals. Percent changes in FLAIR and enhancing volume correlated significantly at 6 weeks (p = 0.004) and 3 months (p < 0.001). FER trended differently between RN and recurrent tumor with patients who developed radiation necrosis (RN) having significantly lower FLAIR volumes at 6 weeks compared to those with recurrent tumor. Baseline lesion size, FLAIR volume, FER (all p < 0.001), primary cancer type, and sex (both p = 0.02) influenced FLAIR trajectories. Conclusions Perilesional edema and enhancement trajectories after SRS are variable but may help distinguish RN from recurrent tumor, particularly at early follow-up. Incorporation of automated edema volumetry should be considered in routine post-SRS surveillance.

title: MRI-based preoperative WHO grade prediction in meningioma: development and comparison of deep learning, radiomics, clinical, and combined models in multicenter data.
abstract: Purpose The objective of this study was to develop and externally validate complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models and their stacked combinations for preoperative World Health Organization (WHO) grading of intracranial meningioma. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 455 histopathologically confirmed meningiomas: a four-center development cohort (n = 346) with leave-one-center-out cross-validation and an external cohort (n = 109). Four base models used contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI: tumor + peritumoral radiomics, an nnU-Net segmentation-based classifier, frozen DINOv3 transfer-learning features, and clinical variables. All 15 combinations were prespecified and stacked using a linear meta-learner trained on development out-of-fold predictions. Frozen models were externally evaluated without modification. Results WHO 2-3 tumors comprised 24.6% overall (112/455; development 20.5%; external 37.6%). External AUCs were 0.732 for nnU-Net, 0.703 for DINOv3, 0.645 for clinical, 0.628 for radiomics. The multimodal ensemble (nnU-Net+DINOv3+Clinical) achieved the highest external AUC (0.742), exceeding radiomics (ΔAUC +0.114, p = 0.008) but not nnU-Net (ΔAUC +0.011, p = 0.737). Compared with the clinical model, discrimination was higher but nonsignificant at the prespecified threshold (ΔAUC +0.098, p = 0.050), while reclassification improved (IDI +0.109, p < 0.001). Radiomics-containing combinations performed strongly in development but lost most discrimination externally. The multimodal ensemble had an external calibration slope of 1.32 (Brier 0.190) and net benefit above default strategies at thresholds ≥ 0.23. Conclusion The multimodal ensemble achieved the highest external AUC but did not significantly exceed nnU-Net, which was the most transportable single predictor of meningioma grade. Clinical variables did not improve discrimination but enabled interpretable feature-level attribution. Handcrafted radiomics lacked external transportability.

title: Radiological features of peritumoral brain injury and neurological outcomes after glioma surgery: a prospective observational study.
abstract: Purpose Despite significant advances in glioma surgery, early postoperative neuroimaging frequently reveals signs of surgical brain injury (SBI). This prospective observational study aimed to investigate the incidence, radiological characteristics, neurological outcomes and risk factors of SBI following glioma resection. Methods Patients with newly diagnosed supratentorial gliomas who undergo tumor resection were prospectively enrolled. Serial MRI examinations were administrated early postoperative (≤ 72 h) and on postoperative days 7, 14 and 28 to assess the characteristics of infarction, edema and microhemorrhage. Neurological outcomes were evaluated using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at postoperative day 28. Results A total of 64 patients was included. Postoperative infarction was identified in 14 patients (21.9%), with all anatomically localized to the basal ganglia, thalamus, or insular regions. Intraoperative blood loss ≥ 300 mL was independently associated with postoperative infarction (Odd Ratio [OR]: 4.62, p = 0.035). Microhemorrhage was observed in 53.8% of patients. Peritumoral edema occurred in all cases and exhibited two distinct patterns: residual tumor-associated edema (n = 42) and de novo surgery-induced edema (n = 22). The average volume of tumor-associated edema decreased, whereas that of surgery-induced edema increased over time. Among the 53 patients who completed neurological outcome assessments, 13 developed disability (mRS ≥ 2). Risk factors were higher intraoperative blood loss (OR: 8.88, p = 0.013) and postoperative infarction (OR: 6.33, p = 0.031). Conclusion SBI, including infarction and edema, is common following glioma surgery and associated with adverse neurological outcomes. Meticulous intraoperative hemostatic management is essential to prevent postoperative infarction and even disability outcome.

title: Volumetric discordance between ¹⁸F-FET-PET/MRI and MRI-based radiotherapy target volumes in high-grade glioma: a prospective pilot study (FETSMaRT).
abstract: Purpose High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. Methods FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. Results Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs. 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs. 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs. 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%). Conclusion FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; the hypothesis generating exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. NCT06499831.

title: Artificial intelligence in gamma knife radiosurgery: applications in treatment planning, response prediction, and toxicity assessment.
abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being developed across the Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) workflow, but its current applications and readiness for clinical integration remain underutilized. This narrative review examines the emerging role of AI in GKRS, with emphasis on treatment planning, outcome prediction, and post-treatment assessment. Methods A structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was conducted through September 20, 2026 to identify studies applying learning-based AI approaches specifically to GKRS. Eligible studies evaluated AI models using GKRS clinical, imaging, or treatment-planning data, while non-GKRS and non-learning-based studies were excluded. Included studies were synthesized according to major stages of the GKRS workflow. Results AI applications were identified across tumor segmentation, isocenter selection and treatment planning, prescription and dose-distribution prediction, synthetic computed tomography generation, and plan-quality assessment. Post-treatment applications include longitudinal tumor monitoring and prediction of response, functional outcomes, and toxicity including peritumoral edema and radiation necrosis. Several models demonstrate promising performance, but the evidence remains predominantly retrospective and task-specific, with frequent reliance on single-center or small datasets and limited external or prospective validation. Conclusion AI has the potential to improve the consistency, efficiency, and personalization of GKRS by supporting specific technical and clinical decisions. Further multicenter validation, prospective evaluation, workflow integration, and demonstration of meaningful clinical benefit are required before routine adoption. AI currently remains a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for radiosurgical expertise.

title: Postoperative DWI morphology and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Purpose To assess whether the association between postoperative diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) and neurological worsening after eloquent-area glioma surgery differs according to lesion morphology. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 139 consecutive patients undergoing resection of eloquent-area supratentorial gliomas (WHO 2-4). Postoperative MRI (< 48 h) classified lesions as sector- or rim-shaped. Neurological status was assessed at discharge and 4-6 months. Results DWI lesions occurred in 44/139 patients (31.7%; 31 sector-shaped, 13 rim-shaped); 59 (42.4%) worsened at discharge. Overall, DWI positivity alone was not associated with worsening. Sector-shaped DWI lesions were associated with neurological worsening (positive predictive value, PPV of 58.1%) and remained associated after multivariable adjustment (OR 3.83, 95% CI 1.30-11.29), although the confidence interval was wide and the unadjusted association was borderline. Rim-shaped lesions carried a PPV of 38.5%, comparable to the risk in DWI-negative patients (37.9%), and the two morphologies did not differ significantly in direct comparison. Awake craniotomy was also independently associated with worsening, and frontal site with a lower risk. 61% of worsening occurred with negative DWI. A deficit was present at the 4-6 month follow-up in 9 patients (6.5%), all with IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, and was associated with a ≥ 50% evoked-potential decrease. Conclusion In this cohort, postoperative DWI positivity was associated with neurological worsening mainly when the lesion was sector-shaped, a finding that requires confirmation in larger series. Rim-shaped lesions showed a risk of worsening similar to that of a negative scan. Most worsening occurs without DWI ischemia, suggesting non-ischemic mechanisms of function-guided surgery. A deficit at follow-up occurred only in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma and was associated with intraoperative neurophysiological changes.

title: Incidence of intra-axial brain metastases in Eastern Finland.
abstract: Purpose Brain metastases (BM) incidence and characteristics remain poorly defined due to registry data being often incomplete, recording only primary tumors or unspecified metastases. The objective of this study was to examine BM incidence rates and characteristics confirmed by MRI in North Savo, Finland. Methods In this retrospective study, North Savo residents with first MRI diagnosis of BM between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023 were identified through the radiology information system, irrespective of primary cancer diagnosis date. Medical and histopathological records were reviewed. Population person-years were estimated by summing annual end-year counts of all North Savo residents obtained from Statistics Finland. Crude incidence rates and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIRs), standardized to the 2013 European Standard population, were calculated. Temporal trends were assessed using age-adjusted Poisson regression. Results Among 516 patients, 474 had histopathological verification. Cancers originating from lung and breast tissue accounted for 56.8% of BM cases. Overall crude incidence was 10.22 (95% CI 9.36-11.15) and ASIR was 9.20 (95% CI 8.42-10.04) per 100,000 person years. ASIR increased from 5.8 in 2004-2008 to 11.8 in 2019-2023. Age-adjusted Poisson regression estimated a 24% increase in incidence per five-year period (incidence rate ratio 1.24; 95% CI 1.14-1.34; P < 0.001). Age-specific incidence peaked at 33.1 per 100,000 person years among patients aged 70-74 years. Conclusions MRI-confirmed BM incidence increased over 20 years, despite age standardization. Incidence was highest among older adults. These findings provide contemporary population-based epidemiological data of BM incidence.

title: GATA3-positive silent corticotroph adenomas are characterized by large size and massive infrasellar invasion.
abstract: Purpose A subgroup of GATA3-positive silent corticotroph adenomas (SCA) was identified by transcriptomics. We aimed to compare clinical, radiological and surgical outcomes of SCA with and without GATA3. Methods Tumor volume calculated using Di Chiro-Nelson formula; microcystic appearance defined as small areas of marked hyperintensity on T2W. Cavernous sinus invasion was assessed with Knosp (grades 3-4 considered invasive), and sellar floor invasion by Hardy-Wilson (grade E as massive invasion). Three to six months after surgery, MRI was repeated to evaluate the extent of the surgical resection, and then annually to assess recurrence or tumor progression, and the need for reoperation or radiotherapy. Results Among 45 SCA, 11 (24.4%) were GATA3-positive. The GATA3 patients were more frequently male (72.7% vs. 29.4%, p = 0.016) and had larger tumor volume [34.8 cm 3 (2.8-130.8) vs. 11.2 cm 3 (3.4-89.8), p = 0.023]. Notably, 81.8% of the GATA3-positive SCA were giant adenomas compared to 24.2% in the other group (p = 0.001), with higher frequency of sphenoid invasion (60% vs. 10.3%, p = 0.004), but with no difference in cavernous sinus invasion (p = 0.299). Gross total resection was less frequent in the GATA3-positive SCA (0% vs. 32.2%, p = 0.041). No difference was seen regarding age, microcystic aspect, granulation pattern, Ki-67, mitoses and post-surgical outcome. Conclusion About one quarter of SCA displayed GATA3-positivity and was seen more frequently in men. GATA3-positive SCA are characterized by large tumor size and massive infrasellar invasion, but not aggressive features as no differences in post-surgical outcomes were detected in our cohort.
