title: Non-contrast CT radiomics for identifying nonfunctioning kidneys: a multicenter development and external validation study.
abstract: Purpose In urological practice, the decision to resect or preserve a kidney with obstruction, tumor or atrophy is based on split renal function, although SPECT renal dynamic scintigraphy as the reference standard is resource-intensive. We developed and externally validated a non-contrast CT radiomics model to identify nonfunctioning kidneys and support urological decision-making in this setting. Methods In this three-center retrospective study (TRIPOD+AI), adults underwent non-contrast CT and SPECT renal dynamic scintigraphy within 72 h. IBSI-compliant radiomics features were extracted with PyRadiomics, and between-kidney asymmetry features were constructed. After three-stage selection (Spearman, recursive feature elimination, and LASSO), 12 machine learning models were developed and externally validated in 2 independent cohorts. A Rad-score and clinical nomogram were also derived. Results Among 1029 patients, the internal cohort included 418 patients. Twenty-three of features were retained. The random forest model yielded an internal test AUC of 0.9426, sensitivity of 85.5%, specificity of 88.3%, and negative predictive value of 95.6%. Its external AUCs were 0.875 and 0.913. The nomogram attained external AUCs of 0.920 and 0.881. At the thresholds fixed in the training data, the random forest achieved external sensitivity of 66.0 and 76.4% with negative predictive values of 94.8 and 93.3%, and the nomogram 92.5 and 93.7% with 98.3 and 97.2%. Both radiomics models outperformed logistic-regression baselines built from clinical variables and simple CT size and asymmetry measurements, although the margin over the combined baseline was not statistically significant in one external cohort. The Rad-score was correlated with single-kidney GFR (ρ = -0.738, P < 0.001) and facilitated risk stratification. Conclusion Non-contrast CT radiomics identified nonfunctioning kidneys without contrast agents or radiotracers. Because non-contrast CT is already part of routine urological workup, this externally validated rule-out tool may reduce unnecessary SPECT examinations and support decisions between nephrectomy and nephron-sparing management.

title: Management of volumetric muscle loss in a dog using bioactive glass-alginate-cellulose composite and a transpositional flap: a case report.
abstract: This case report describes the management of a complex volumetric muscle loss (VML) injury in a 3-year-old mixed-breed dog following severe trauma to the right forelimb, which resulted in extensive multi-muscle defects that were unsuitable for primary closure. After initial stabilization and surgical debridement, reconstruction was achieved using a transpositional flap, while a gold nanoparticles-bioactive glass-alginate-cellulose (BGAuSP-Alg-MCC) composite was implanted to fill the dead space and support tissue regeneration. Postoperative healing was evaluated through clinical follow-up, computed tomography performed immediately and at 1 and 3 months postoperatively, as well as histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Imaging demonstrated progressive integration of the biomaterial, restoration of tissue density comparable to adjacent muscle, and absence of major complications. Histological evaluation demonstrated moderate inflammation and granulation tissue formation, containing numerous blood capillaries (neoangiogenesis), confirmed by CD31 and α-Smooth muscle actin (SMA) immunolabelling. Functional recovery was favorable, with preserved limb mobility and normal gait. These findings provide preliminary evidence of local biocompatibility and support the feasibility of incorporating the BGAuSP-Alg-MCC composite into a multimodal surgical management approach for extensive volumetric muscle loss in canine patients.

title: From traditional histopathology to virtual staining: deep learning approaches for assessing tissue lesions in farmed fish.
abstract: Pesticides in aquaculture water and feed primarily induce chronic, sublethal toxicity rather than acute mortality, impairing growth, immune function, and tissue integrity. Consequently, organ-specific histopathological biomarkers are essential for ecotoxicological assessment and welfare monitoring. Traditional histopathology directly evaluates structural damage in key organs (e.g., gills, liver, kidneys). However, manual workflows face major bottlenecks, including invasive sampling, labor-intensive preparation, and observer-dependent scoring that hinder high-throughput screening and regulatory harmonization. This review evaluates how digital pathology integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), deep learning for automated lesion quantification, and generative AI-based virtual staining bridges these analytical gaps. We examine how digitalization enhances diagnostic objectivity and scalability while reducing scoring variability. Furthermore, we critically address key implementation challenges, including ground-truth requirements, domain shifts across staining protocols, species generalization, and dataset annotation burdens. Ultimately, AI-enabled digital pathology represents a credible pathway toward objective, high-throughput pesticide toxicity assessment in aquaculture. However, standardized validation frameworks and robust ground-truth datasets remain critical prerequisites before these tools can transition from experimental promise to regulatory acceptance.

title: Deep Learning-based Synthesis of Amyloid PET Images from Structural MRI in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Rationale Amyloid-beta (Aβ) plaques in Alzheimer's disease (AD) are commonly imaged with specific PET radiotracers. To overcome the cost and availability limitations of PET, developing a more accessible diagnostic tool is essential. This study aimed to develop a deep-learning model that can synthesize Aβ-PET images from widely available MRI scans. Methods The study utilized 431 subjects with both structural MRI and Aβ-PET scans from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database, including 213 cognitively normal (CN), 180 mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 38 AD dementia cases. A specialized Vector Quantized Generative Adversarial Network (VQGAN) framework has been trained to generate Aβ-PET images from MRI features, utilizing datasets from patients across various stages of AD spectrum. A paired t-test was used to compare synthetic and real Aβ-PET scans, while an ANOVA was performed to evaluate standardized uptake value ratio differences among the CN, MCI, and AD dementia groups. Results The synthesized Aβ-PET images closely resemble real Aβ-PET scans in terms of regional Aβ distribution, accurately capturing disease-stage characteristics across the AD spectrum. In three key cortical brain regions (frontal cortex, lateral temporal lobe, and posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus), the synthetic images have successfully replicated disease-related Aβ trends, showing statistically significant group differences (p < 0.05). Quantitative evaluation has confirmed the superiority of VQGAN over other models (lower MAE, higher PSNR/SSIM), demonstrating minimized errors, reduced noise, and better structural fidelity in synthesized images. Conclusion This technology potentially offers a cost-effective, non-invasive alternative method for AD diagnosis and staging.

title: Deep learning-based automated scanline localization in suprahyoid muscle ultrasound for quantitative dysphagia assessment.
abstract: Ultrasound-based assessment of suprahyoid muscle (SHM) motion has emerged as a promising approach for evaluating dysphagia. However, quantitative analysis remains limited by operator-dependent scanline placement and variability in manual interpretation. This study proposes an integrated framework combining mathematical modeling, automated SHM segmentation, scanline determination, and deep learning-based analysis for objective dysphagia assessment. A total of 371 ultrasound images acquired from patients with normal, mild, and severe dysphagia were analyzed. Clinically relevant SHM-derived variables, including thickness, displacement, SHM Difference (Δ = D - T), and total duration, were incorporated into a mathematical interpretation framework. U-Net was employed for SHM segmentation and automatic scanline determination, and agreement with expert-selected scanlines was evaluated using median-based accuracy, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), mean pairwise absolute difference (MPAD), and population standard deviation (SDpop). In addition, five deep learning architectures (ResNet-101, Fast R-CNN, YOLO11, VGG-19, and U-Net) were compared for dysphagia severity classification. The proposed framework demonstrated high agreement with expert assessments. U-Net achieved an average intersection-over-union (IoU) of 0.9599 across the three major SHM components, indicating near-expert segmentation performance. Automated scanline determination achieved an overall agreement of 72.3% with expert consensus, while manual scanline placement exhibited relatively low interobserver reliability (ICC = 0.386). Among the evaluated classification models, Fast R-CNN achieved the highest performance with an F1-score of 0.993 and an inference time of 3.44 ms. Grad-CAM analysis further confirmed that model attention was concentrated on clinically relevant SHM regions. The proposed framework provides an objective and reproducible approach for ultrasound-based dysphagia assessment by integrating mathematical modeling with AI-driven segmentation and classification. Automated SHM localization and scanline determination reduce operator dependency while maintaining expert-level accuracy. These findings support the potential of AI-assisted ultrasound as a clinically applicable tool for standardized dysphagia evaluation and real-time decision support.

title: Robust cross-anatomy image registration leveraging keypoint priors and contour-based assessment.
abstract: Accurate registration between lateral cephalometric radiographs and facial profile photographs is a prerequisite for integrated craniofacial analysis, yet it remains challenging due to inherent modality gaps and the absence of clinically validated evaluation criteria. This study presents a clinically-driven engineering framework that systematically integrates high-resolution keypoint localization with a weighted Procrustes-based two-dimensional similarity registration. The uniform scale factor accommodates global magnification differences between imaging modalities, while shearing and local non-rigid deformation are excluded. To ensure clinical interpretability, we incorporate expert-defined anatomical priors as weights into the transformation process and introduce an adaptive seed-driven contour tracking (ASDCT) algorithm for precise performance evaluation. Experiments on 198 paired clinical samples demonstrate that our framework achieves stable performance (Contour Distance of 3.52 pixels; Contour Dilation Overlap of 87%) and provides metrics that correlate strongly with expert clinical assessments. By unifying landmark-guided alignment and boundary-consistency evaluation, this framework offers a robust, reproducible, and anatomically reliable solution for cross-modal craniofacial integration, effectively bridging the gap between computational precision and clinical practice.

This study presents a clinically-driven engineering framework that systematically integrates high-resolution keypoint localization with a weighted Procrustes-based two-dimensional similarity registration. The uniform scale factor accommodates global magnification differences between imaging modalities, while shearing and local non-rigid deformation are excluded. To ensure clinical interpretability, we incorporate expert-defined anatomical priors as weights into the transformation process and introduce an adaptive seed-driven contour tracking (ASDCT) algorithm for precise performance evaluation. title: HSF-Net: a hybrid-scale fusion network for intracranial aneurysm segmentation in CTA images.
abstract: Rupture of intracranial aneurysms is a major cause of subarachnoid hemorrhage, making accurate segmentation important for aneurysm assessment and treatment planning. However, automated segmentation in computed tomography angiography (CTA) remains challenging because of small lesion size, complex morphology, and ambiguous boundaries between aneurysms and adjacent vessels. To address these challenges, we propose HSF-Net, a Swin UNETR-based segmentation network that integrates a Hybrid-Scale Fusion (HSF) module and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) into the decoder. Unlike conventional decoders that mainly rely on simple feature concatenation, HSF-Net follows a "fuse first, refine later" strategy, in which HSF performs input-dependent multi-scale feature fusion and CBAM subsequently refines the fused features through channel and spatial attention. On the internal independent test set, HSF-Net achieved a mean patient-level Dice score of 83.4%, outperforming the Swin UNETR baseline and obtaining the highest Dice score among the evaluated methods under the same evaluation protocol. Ablation studies confirmed the complementary contributions of HSF and CBAM. Evaluation on an independent external cohort provided preliminary evidence of its cross-center applicability. These results suggest that HSF-Net provides an effective approach for automated intracranial aneurysm segmentation in CTA images.

title: Segmenting scaffolds with ingrown bone in micro-CT images: considerations of evaluation metrics and loss functions.
abstract: U-Net models are useful for biomedical image segmentation because they do not require large training sets. Here, we trained three U-Net models, each with a different loss function, to segment micro-CT image patches of scaffolds with ingrown bone to quantify bone growth fraction. Segmentation performance is typically reported using metrics like Accuracy, DSC, Precision, and Recall. However, these metrics did not reflect performance relative to the application's key output measure. We therefore aimed to establish an application-specific parameter, ΔBGF: the difference in bone growth fraction (BGF) between predicted output (PO) and ground truth (GT). Bland-Altman analysis showed small systematic bias (< 1.5 percentage points), supporting PO-GT agreement. Accuracy was the metric most strongly correlated to |ΔBGF| in nearly all comparisons (Steiger test), and this relationship was stable under bootstrap resampling. The models were robust to changes in orientation, resolution, and contrast, supporting broader generalizability. The cross-entropy loss model generated the most reliable segmentation. PO-GT error was small relative to meaningful biological differences, suggesting it is unlikely to affect future treatment comparisons. Overall, standard metrics can be misleading, while ΔBGF provides a reliable, application-specific measure of performance for this still developing use of U-Net in quantifying bone regeneration.

title: RDB CycleGAN-CBAM: an integrated deep learning model for low-dose ct image denoising.
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) is one of the largest contributors to radiation exposure from medical imaging, which can induce DNA damage and increase cancer risk. Reducing CT radiation dose to improve patient safety inherently increases image noise and artifacts. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown promise for unsupervised low-dose CT (LDCT) denoising. Building on this, RDBCycleGAN-CBAM, a CycleGAN-based model that integrates residual dense blocks (RDBs) and convolutional block attention modules (CBAM), was developed to effectively denoise quarter-dose CT images while preserving structural detail. The model was trained on unpaired quarter-dose and full-dose CT scans from the NIH-AAPM-Mayo dataset using adversarial (LSGAN), cycle-consistency, and identity losses. Evaluation on held-out test slices was performed using PSNR and SSIM as the primary image-quality metrics. The results demonstrate that the proposed RDBCycleGAN-CBAM method demonstrated improvements that were competitive with values reported in previous studies, achieving mean improvements of + 3.973 dB in PSNR and + 0.053 in SSIM relative to quarter-dose inputs. Shapiro-Wilk tests for PSNR and SSIM motivated the use of the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test, by which highly significant improvements across both metrics (PSNR and SSIM) were demonstrated. The very large rank-biserial correlation values (1.0) indicate that nearly all test images experienced substantial quality improvement. Furthermore, the narrow bootstrap confidence intervals for the mean differences suggest that these improvements are consistent across the dataset. These findings support further investigation of RDBCycleGAN-CBAM as a vendor-neutral image-domain denoising approach, while external validation and reader studies are required to establish its clinical utility and potential for dose reduction.

title: Curriculum-guided adaptive representation decoupling for multimodal semi-supervised chest disease classification.
abstract: Chest diseases remain a major source of morbidity and mortality, while automated chest X-ray diagnosis is constrained by annotation scarcity and heterogeneous clinical information. Frontal and lateral radiographs provide complementary views within one X-ray modality, whereas pre-diagnostic clinical context constitutes a heterogeneous textual modality. We propose Curriculum-guided Adaptive Representation Decoupling (CARD) for multimodal semi-supervised chest disease classification. Label-aware Dynamic Curriculum Learning combines prediction persistence with dynamic confidence thresholds to partition unlabeled sample-label pairs into easy, stable, and hard groups. Persistence-guided Adaptive Feature Decoupling transfers these reliability cues to cross-view representation learning. It balances view-consistent alignment against preservation of projection-specific radiographic information. The learned multi-view radiographic representation is then fused with clinical-text features for multimodal prediction. Under the matched radiographic protocol, CARD achieved a Macro-AUROC of 75.9%, exceeding STiL by 1.1 percentage points. Adding matched pre-diagnostic clinical text increased Macro-AUROC to 77.0%. These findings support reliability-aware curriculum learning, adaptive cross-view representation decoupling, and clinically aligned multimodal fusion.

title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
abstract: Background Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification. Methods In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). Results Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). Conclusion The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment. Clinical trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

Background

Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification.

Methods

In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).

Results

Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73).

Conclusion

The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment.

title: A two-stage model combining clinical and delta-radiomics features for prognosis in high-grade gliomas after chemoradiotherapy: a retrospective study.
abstract: Objective This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of integrating pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy radiomics, temporal changes in tumor radiomics (delta radiomics) during chemoradiotherapy, and clinical variables into prognostic models for individualized overall survival (OS) prediction in patients with high-grade glioma (HGG). Methods A total of 143 patients with HGG who underwent standard chemoradiotherapy were retrospectively enrolled from two centers. Patients were divided into a training cohort (n = 116), in which 5-fold cross-validation was performed, and an external test cohort (n = 27). Radiomics features were extracted from pre-radiotherapy and mid-radiotherapy MRI scans, and delta radiomic features were calculated as the differences between the two timepoints. Feature selection was performed using elastic-net-based stability selection, and radiomics scores (Rad-scores) were generated for each selected feature set using Cox models. Rad-scores were subsequently combined with clinical variables in a random survival forest (RSF) model for OS prediction. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis was performed to evaluate prognostic stratification. Results The combined model integrating clinical variables and delta radiomics achieved a C-index of 0.818 and 0.761 in the validation and external test cohorts, respectively, outperforming models based solely on radiomics or clinical features. In the external test cohort, time-dependent discrimination yielded 12-, 18-, 24- and 30-month OS AUCs of 0.842, 0.856, 0.796, and 0.943, and Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significant risk stratification (p = 0.002). Conclusion The findings of this retrospective study suggest that integrating multi-timepoint radiomics, delta radiomics features, and clinical variables may facilitate OS prediction in patients with HGG following standard chemoradiotherapy. While promising, the exploratory findings require further validation in larger prospective cohorts, given the limited size of the external validation cohort and the absence of MGMT promoter methylation status from the main model.

title: The evolution of image-guided ablations for thyroid disorders: a historical review.
abstract: Over the past four decades, the management of thyroid nodules and selected thyroid malignancies has progressively shifted from surgery-centered approaches toward image-guided minimally invasive treatments (MITT). What began in 1985 with ultrasound-guided percutaneous ethanol injection evolved into a range of energy-based techniques, including laser ablation (LA), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation (MWA), and high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU).This historical review aimed to reconstruct the major milestones in the development of image-guided thyroid ablation. A systematic PubMed literature search and predefined selection criteria were used to identify seminal studies, first clinical applications, major technological innovations, comparative studies, guideline-defining publications, and landmark long-term follow-up studies. Overall, 43 milestone papers were included for qualitative historical analysis. The evolution of thyroid ablation can be divided into five phases: conceptual origins (1985-1999), birth of the thermal procedures' era (2000-2006), methodological standardization (2007-2012), oncologic consolidation and comparative evidence (2013-2018), and final codification by means of international guideline endorsement and long-term validation (2019-2025). Recent 10-year follow-up studies have confirmed the durable efficacy of MITT for benign nodule management and their sustained oncologic control in low-risk papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. Image-guided thyroid ablation has transitioned from experimental innovation to an evidence-based, guideline-supported therapeutic domain, representing a paradigm shift toward precision medicine, organ preservation, and minimally invasive endocrine oncology.

title: Learning from the unseen: synthetic data for scoliosis AI segmentation.
abstract: Purpose Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce. Methods We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset. Results On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable. Conclusion Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce.

Methods

We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset.

Results

On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable.

Conclusion

Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.

title: Resection zone prediction for parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy planning: a comparative study of three modeling paradigms.
abstract: Purpose Parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy planning depends on accurate resection zones that preserve functional liver tissue without compromising oncological margins. This work investigates how different levels of anatomical and functional information complexity influence resection zone prediction for parenchyma-sparing surgical planning for primary liver cancer. Methods We compare three modeling paradigms: a geometric distance-based approach, an explicit perfusion-based method using vascular anatomy, and a deep learning-based model built on the U-Net architecture. All methods operate on segmentation-derived representations of the liver, tumor, and vessels. Performance is evaluated using overlap- and distance-based metrics. Results The distance-based model produces predictions with limited surface deviation (HD 95 33.89 mm) but lower overlap due to undersegmentation (DSC 58.18 %). The perfusion-based method achieves a favorable balance between overlap (DSC 67.41 %) and boundary accuracy (HD 95 37.92 mm) but tends to overestimate the predicted region due to strict binary perfusion assumptions. The deep learning model attains the highest overlap accuracy (DSC 76.31 %) while exhibiting larger distance errors (HD 95 65.21 mm), reflecting localized boundary inaccuracies. Conclusion None of the models is universally outperforming the other two for parenchyma-sparing resection planning. Deep learning shows strong predictive performance, particularly for larger resection volumes, while geometric and perfusion-based models offer greater interpretability and clinical controllability. The distance-based approach is well suited for maximal parenchyma-sparing resections, whereas perfusion-based modeling is advantageous for tumors near vessels with potential perfusion loss. Our results highlight variations due to different surgical strategies and can thus provide valuable guidance for individual patient's surgery planning.

title: Improving the fairness and robustness of deep learning classification models through bias mitigation and post hoc calibration.
abstract: Purpose The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer's disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations. Methods Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. We evaluated model performance, fairness, and calibration using classification as well as calibration-specific metrics. Results PMDN achieved the best overall performance, with higher balanced accuracy (0.71) and improved calibration (Brier ≈ 0.22), showing substantially reduced variability compared to baseline and CF-Net. PMDN effectively removed age-related bias, achieving near-zero age prediction correlation; CF-Net, however, showed only partial and unstable debiasing. Post hoc calibration further improved probability reliability, with nonparametric methods (isotonic regression and Bayesian binning) yielding the lowest calibration errors (MCE ≈ 0.21-0.24). Conclusion This study shows that, although deep learning models achieve similar classification performance, they differ significantly in terms of calibration, stability, and fairness. PMDN provides more consistent and effective age bias mitigation than the CF-Net approach, particularly in clinically relevant subgroups. Post hoc calibration improves probability reliability further, with nonparametric methods achieving the best calibration.

title: Multimodal neuroimaging in dementia and neurodegenerative disorders: complementary roles of clinically available nuclear medicine and MRI in the era of disease-modifying therapies.
abstract: The introduction of anti-amyloid-β antibody therapies has fundamentally changed the clinical landscape of dementia, shifting the role of neuroimaging from diagnosis toward therapeutic decision-making. Amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) has become essential for confirming amyloid pathology and determining treatment eligibility. However, amyloid deposition is frequently observed in cognitively normal elderly individuals and in non-Alzheimer neurodegenerative disorders, indicating that amyloid status alone is insufficient to explain clinical symptoms. In this context, imaging modalities reflecting neurodegeneration, including structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and functional imaging such as 18 F-FDG-PET and brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), remain important for assessing disease severity and functional impairment. Furthermore, discrepancies between imaging biomarkers-such as the presence of neurodegeneration without amyloid pathology in cases clinically suspected of Alzheimer's disease, and atypical imaging patterns-are commonly encountered in clinical practice and may reflect underlying pathological heterogeneity. A multimodal imaging approach that integrates multiple biomarkers provides complementary information and may improve diagnostic accuracy and clinical interpretation. In addition, other imaging modalities, including dopamine transporter (DAT) imaging and cardiac sympathetic imaging, can contribute to the evaluation of non-Alzheimer pathologies. This review summarizes the current roles of clinically available multimodal imaging in dementia, with a focus on nuclear medicine and MRI, highlighting their complementary value and clinical implications in the era of disease-modifying therapies.

title: MRI and proton MR spectroscopy in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a comprehensive imaging review.
abstract: Neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) remains a leading cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental disability. Although cranial ultrasound is widely used as a bedside screening tool, brain MRI has become central to diagnosis, injury pattern classification, timing estimation, and outcome prediction. Furthermore, proton MR spectroscopy ( 1 H-MRS) provides complementary metabolic biomarkers that enhance prognostication. This review focuses on MRI and 1 H-MRS in neonatal encephalopathy due to hypoxic-ischemic injury, addressing both term and preterm infants. The pathophysiologic determinants of injury distribution are summarized, the optimal timing of imaging and diffusion evolution is discussed, and practical acquisition protocols including recommended sequences and 1 H-MRS parameters are proposed. Key MRI phenotypes in term infants-basal ganglia-thalamus injury, watershed/parasagittal cortical-subcortical injury, and global or near-total injury patterns are reviewed with attention to common pitfalls such as diffusion pseudonormalization and evolving T1/T2 signal changes. For preterm infants, this review highlights distinctive vulnerabilities of the germinal matrix and periventricular white matter, emphasizing the spectrum from punctate white matter injury (WMI) to cystic periventricular leukomalacia (PVL). For 1 H-MRS, voxel selection, echo time considerations, and interpretation of lactate, N-acetylaspartate (NAA), choline, creatine, and myo-inositol are detailed. Evidence suggests that deep gray matter lactate/NAA or NAA-based metrics serve as reliable and robust outcome biomarkers. Emerging directions including arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion are also discussed.

title: Atypical ovarian fibroma and thecoma mimicking malignancy: clue for differentiation from malignant solid tumors.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the characteristic findings of ovarian fibroma and thecoma (FT) with atypical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings that mimic malignancy and to validate the improvement in diagnostic performance in differentiating between FTs and malignant solid tumors. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 114 patients (119 lesions: 34 FT and 85 malignant tumors) with pathologically confirmed solid ovarian tumors who underwent preoperative MRI. Signal intensity on T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) maps, and time-intensity curves from dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) were evaluated. FT lesions showing low signal intensity on both T2WI and DWI were defined as classic, whereas others were considered atypical. The diagnostic performance of combined imaging findings was also assessed. A reader study was also performed by three radiologists. Results Among the FT lesions, 55.9% demonstrated intermediate signal intensity on T2WI, and 32.4% showed diffusion restriction. Atypical FT accounted for 56% of all FT cases. The combination of T2WI and DWI showed high specificity (98.8%) but low sensitivity (44.1%) for diagnosing FT as benign. In contrast, for the diagnosis of benign lesions, the combination of T2WI and DCE-MRI demonstrated superior diagnostic performance, with a sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value of 84.0%, 95.9%, 87.5%, and 94.6%, respectively. Reader performance improved when the combined interpretation of T2WI and DCE-MRI findings was emphasized. Using this approach, the estimated misdiagnosis rate of FT as malignant decreased from approximately 40% to 16%. Conclusion Atypical FT frequently mimics malignant ovarian tumors on MRI. The combination of T2WI and DCE-MRI findings provides the best diagnostic performance and significantly reduces misdiagnosis. However, a subset of FT remains indistinguishable from malignancy, highlighting the need for careful interpretation.

title: Comparison of PMAneo and RAPID in acute ischemic stroke: agreement in CT perfusion analysis and DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility.
abstract: Purpose Automated computed tomography perfusion (CTP) analysis plays a key role in triaging acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to evaluate the agreement of PMAneo compared with RAPID in a multicenter setting. Materials and methods We retrospectively reviewed 99 patients with anterior circulation AIS from three stroke centers using four different CT scanners. CTP data were processed using both PMAneo and RAPID. Volumetric agreement for ischemic core volume and Tmax > 6 s volume was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland-Altman analysis. Multivariable regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with volume discrepancies. EVT imaging eligibility was evaluated according to the DEFUSE 3 criteria (ischemic core volume < 70 mL, mismatch ratio ≥ 1.8, and absolute mismatch volume ≥ 15 mL), using RAPID as the comparator. Results Ischemic core volumes showed excellent agreement between the two platforms (ICC = 0.881, 95% CI 0.827-0.918), and Tmax > 6 s volumes showed good agreement (ICC = 0.761, 95% CI 0.283-0.896), whereas mismatch volumes showed moderate agreement (ICC = 0.661, 95% CI 0.146-0.844). For the ischemic core threshold (< 70 mL), PMAneo demonstrated 100% (95% CI 96-100%) relative sensitivity and 67% (95% CI 38-88%) relative specificity. For the full DEFUSE 3 criteria, the relative sensitivity and specificity were 81% (95% CI 70-89%) and 84% (95% CI 66-95%), respectively. Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated proportional bias, with PMAneo underestimating volumes relative to RAPID as lesion size increased. Basal ganglia involvement and imaging site were significantly associated with these volume differences (p < 0.05). Conclusion PMAneo showed high volumetric agreement and comparable DEFUSE 3 imaging eligibility to RAPID, suggesting it is a reliable alternative for automated CTP analysis. Although proportional bias and potential diagnostic discrepancies were observed in borderline cases near clinically relevant thresholds, PMAneo may facilitate broader access to automated CTP analysis.

EVT imaging eligibility was evaluated according to the DEFUSE 3 criteria (ischemic core volume < 70 mL, mismatch ratio ≥ 1.8, and absolute mismatch volume ≥ 15 mL), using RAPID as the comparator.

title: MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion in locally advanced cervical cancer: association with pathological venous invasion, pretreatment lymph node metastasis, and survival outcomes.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate MRI-defined parametrial venous invasion (mrPMVI) for detecting pathological parametrial venous invasion (pPMVI) and its associations with pretreatment lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 42 patients with cervical cancer with parametrial invasion on MRI or histopathology, corresponding to International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stage IIB or higher disease. Fifteen patients underwent surgery without preoperative therapy and were included in the pathological validation analysis. Image interpretation was primarily based on T2-weighted and diffusion-weighted imaging. Two radiologists independently assessed mrPMVI using a five-point scoring system. Scores ≥ 3 were predefined as mrPMVI-positive. Diagnostic performance for pPMVI and interobserver agreement were evaluated. Univariable logistic and Cox regression analyses were performed for pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, respectively. Results pPMVI was present in 10 of 15 patients. The five-point mrPMVI score showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.60-0.98) for detecting pPMVI. The predefined threshold (≥ 3) yielded 30.0% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Interobserver agreement for the five-point mrPMVI score was substantial (linearly weighted κ = 0.75). mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM (odds ratio = 4.00, 95% CI: 1.05-15.26, p = 0.042). During a median follow-up of 24.0 months, 16 patients experienced disease progression and 10 died. mrPMVI positivity was associated with shorter progression-free survival (hazard ratio = 34.25, 95% CI: 4.35-269.91; p < 0.001) and overall survival (hazard ratio = 10.16; 95% CI: 1.28-80.61, p = 0.028). Conclusion The mrPMVI score showed potential for identifying pPMVI, although the predefined threshold was highly specific but insensitive. mrPMVI positivity was associated with pretreatment LNM and survival outcomes, suggesting potential complementary value for risk characterization in locally advanced cervical cancer.

title: Multiparametric imaging with dynamic 18 F-FDG PET shows increased breast glucose metabolism in patients with breast cancer.
abstract: Multiparametric PET separates tracer signal into bound and free fractions via reconstructions that reflect the net trapping rate (Ki) and apparent distribution volume (DV). This study aimed to investigate differences in background parenchymal uptake (BPU) between patients with and without breast cancer using multiparametric PET and to evaluate differences in primary tumor uptake according to hormone receptor status. This retrospective case-control study included female patients (n = 48) with newly diagnosed breast cancer and 146 patients without breast cancer. Patients with breast cancer under or after treatment and patients with bilateral breast cancer were excluded. Enrolled patients underwent whole-body dynamic PET and three quantitative indices representing BPU (maximum standardized uptake value [SUVmax], Ki and DV) were calculated. The primary tumor uptake was calculated between estrogen- or progesterone-receptor-positive and -negative groups. The mean SUVmax, Ki and DV of breast cancer cases were 1.39 ± 0.352, 4.88 × 10 - 3 ± 1.61 × 10 - 3 and 24.2 ± 15.4 respectively, whereas in control cases, mean SUVmax, Ki and DV were 1.10 ± 0.320, 3.96 × 10 - 3 ± 1.25 × 10 - 3 and 17.1 ± 10.8 respectively (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004). The areas under the curve from the ROC analysis for breast cancer presence were calculated as 0.727, 0.681 and 0.653 respectively. In addition, age-stratified analysis showed that SUVmax and Ki were significantly higher in patients with breast cancer than in patients without breast cancer. Regarding the primary tumor uptake, Ki was significantly higher in the estrogen receptor-positive group. Multiparametric PET revealed that pure glucose metabolism is significantly elevated in the background mammary glands of patients with breast cancer, and the Ki in the primary tumor is associated with ER status. Dynamic PET imaging may be a useful imaging biomarker for the development of breast cancer.

title: Utility of super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction for improving visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma at hepatic dynamic CT: comparison with hybrid iterative reconstruction and conventional deep-learning reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose The aim of this study was to evaluate whether Precise IQ Engine (PIQE), a super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction designed to enhance spatial resolution while reducing image noise using a deep convolutional neural network, improves the visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) compared with hybrid iterative reconstruction (Adaptive Iterative Dose Reduction with three-dimensional processing [AIDR 3D]) and conventional deep-learning reconstruction (Advanced Intelligent Clear-IQ Engine [AiCE]) in hepatic dynamic CT. Methods and materials We evaluated 64 patients with HCC who had undergone hepatic dynamic CT. Hepatic arterial- and equilibrium phase (HAP and EP) scans were reconstructed with AIDR, AiCE, and PIQE. A radiologist measured the standard deviation of attenuation in the liver parenchyma as the image noise and calculated the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) = (ROI T - ROI L )/N in HAP and (ROI L - ROI T )/N in EP. ROI L is the mean attenuation of the liver parenchyma, ROI T the mean tumor attenuation, and N the noise. HCC visibility was assessed by 2 additional radiologists and graded with a focus on tumor margin delineation on a 5-point confidence scale. Results PIQE showed the lowest image noise, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). The CNR of HCCs was highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). Qualitative visibility scores for HCCs were also highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). Conclusion PIQE significantly improves HCC visibility compared with AIDR and AiCE in hepatic dynamic CT, along with reduced image noise and increased CNR.

title: The Diagnostic Yield of Whole-Body MRI as a Multi-disease Screening Modality: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Disease screening is a mainstay of modern healthcare. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (WBMRI) is marketed as a multi-disease screening modality. The diagnostic yield and clinical utility of WBMRI for population-based disease screening are uncertain. Objectives Our systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize and critically appraise the available literature on WBMRI without an evidence-based indication. Our objective was to evaluate the diagnostic yield of WBMRI and assess the scope of findings. Design We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis searching MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from inception through August 2025. This review was registered with PROSPERO (No.: CRD42024554848). Prespecified criteria for study inclusion included literature that reported WBMRI findings in a population without an evidence-based indication for WBMRI. Data appraisal was performed by two independent reviewers with summary data extracted from published reports. Main measures Outcomes evaluated included pooled proportions of individuals with no clinical findings reported, any clinical finding, non-malignant actionable findings that required subsequent diagnostic workup, and new cancer diagnoses. Key results In a pooled cohort of 18,043 individuals from 17 heterogeneous low-quality studies who underwent WBMRI, 16.9% (95% CI 5.1; 43.7) had no findings reported, while 78.0% (95% CI 44.9; 93.9) had a finding reported. Clinically actionable non-malignant findings were reported in 14.8% (95% CI 6.6-30.0%); 58.2% (95% CI 36.0; 77.5) of these individuals pursued additional laboratory work and/or imaging, and 20.8% (95% CI 9.7; 39.2) pursued a subsequent procedure. The prevalence of malignancy was 1.4% (95% CI 0.9-2.2%). Clinical outcomes associated with discovery of lesions could not be determined. Conclusions The majority of WBMRIs performed in a population without an evidence-based indication result in findings that are normal or do not require follow-up. Clinical outcomes associated with discovery of actionable lesions are unknown. High-quality observational data or randomized trials are needed to inform the efficacy of WBMRI for multi-disease screening. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Evidence for Embedding Smoking and Vaping Cessation Support in Primary Care: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Smoking is a leading preventable cause of disease, with vaping creating new public health concerns. This review synthesised evidence on interventions and strategies to integrate cessation care into primary healthcare. Methods We conducted a systematic scoping review of PubMed and EMBASE for studies published between 19 September 2020 and 19 September 2024. Eligible studies evaluated smoking and/or vaping cessation interventions or implementation strategies in primary care settings in high-income countries (Australia, Canada, EU, UK, USA). Two reviewers independently extracted data on study characteristics, intervention types, outcomes, and abstinence verification. Results Of 2166 records screened, 30 empirical studies were included. Most focused on smoking cessation, with only two addressing e-cigarette users. The strongest evidence supported multi-component interventions combining behavioural counselling and pharmacological treatments. Implementation strategies included electronic health record prompts, cost-free pharmacotherapy, financial incentives, and integration of cessation support into low-dose computed tomography screening or post-spirometry feedback. Evidence for the effectiveness of provider education was inconclusive. Conclusions The evidence supports several interventions and implementation strategies for integrating smoking cessation into primary care, though data on vaping cessation are limited. These findings will inform the development of targeted approaches to enhance cessation support in primary healthcare.

Methods

We conducted a systematic scoping review of PubMed and EMBASE for studies published between 19 September 2020 and 19 September 2024. Eligible studies evaluated smoking and/or vaping cessation interventions or implementation strategies in primary care settings in high-income countries (Australia, Canada, EU, UK, USA). Two reviewers independently extracted data on study characteristics, intervention types, outcomes, and abstinence verification.

Results

Of 2166 records screened, 30 empirical studies were included. Most focused on smoking cessation, with only two addressing e-cigarette users. The strongest evidence supported multi-component interventions combining behavioural counselling and pharmacological treatments. Implementation strategies included electronic health record prompts, cost-free pharmacotherapy, financial incentives, and integration of cessation support into low-dose computed tomography screening or post-spirometry feedback. Evidence for the effectiveness of provider education was inconclusive.

Conclusions

The evidence supports several interventions and implementation strategies for integrating smoking cessation into primary care, though data on vaping cessation are limited. These findings will inform the development of targeted approaches to enhance cessation support in primary healthcare.

title: Cost-utility analysis of deep learning-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening using chest radiographs: implications of diagnostic thresholds and confirmatory testing.
abstract: Osteoporosis often goes undetected until a fracture occurs. Using a deep learning model to analyze routine chest radiographs may cost-effectively identify at-risk individuals. Economic benefit depends on how common the disease is, how the model is calibrated, and whether patients follow through with confirmatory bone density testing and pharmacological treatment initiation. Background Osteoporosis is common among postmenopausal women and often unrecognized until fragility fractures occur, despite its clinical and economic burden. Deep learning (DL)-based opportunistic screening using existing chest radiographs is a potential approach, but its economic value may vary with disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and care pathway completion. Aim To assess the economic value of a DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening approach among Taiwanese postmenopausal women. Methods A cost-utility analysis was conducted from the Taiwan healthcare perspective using a hybrid decision tree and Markov model. The model simulated a cohort of 50-year-old postmenopausal women over a 50-year horizon. Model inputs, including diagnostic performance, long-term outcomes, costs, and utilities, were derived from published literature, preferably local sources. Additional analyses examined alternative prevalence settings, sensitivity and specificity combinations, and confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation rates. Results In the base case, assuming full care-pathway completion, DL-based screening was cost-effective versus no screening, with an ICER of 21,827 per QALY, below the willingness-to-pay threshold of one GDP per capita in Taiwan. The approach became cost-effective when osteoporosis prevalence exceeded 14.3%. Across the diagnostic continuum, a sensitivity of 86.6% and specificity of 76.3% generated the greatest economic benefit. Conclusion DL-based opportunistic osteoporosis screening was cost-effective under full care-pathway implementation. Its value depended on disease prevalence, diagnostic performance, and completion of confirmatory DXA and treatment initiation, and was not maintained under real-world examination estimates observed in Taiwan. Strengthening the post-screening care pathway is therefore central to realizing this value.

title: From voxels to models: a multi-center voxel-based morphometry study identifying robust biomarkers for deep learning classification of schizophrenia.
abstract: Background The application of deep learning in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia has lagged behind neuro-oncology, primarily due to a lack of identifiable neuroanatomical targets and concerns regarding generalizability across sites. Methods To address this, we analyzed structural MRI data from a multi-site study of 401 subjects (194 schizophrenia, 207 healthy) across three independent datasets (COBRE, FBIRN, SLIM). We employed a two-stage conservative voxel-based morphometry (VBM) approach where neuroanatomical regions identified in a discovery dataset (COBRE) were rigorously validated in independent replication datasets (FBIRN, SLIM). The neuroanatomical features that survived this validation were then used to train a support vector machine (SVM) classifier with strictly nested cross-validation to prevent data leakage. Results Fifteen robust structural biomarkers were identified, consistently showing gray matter reductions in frontal and temporal regions, white matter alterations, and ventricular enlargement across all datasets. The SVM classifier achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94 with 89.5% accuracy in initial analysis, with strictly nested cross-validation confirming robust performance (AUC = 0.93, accuracy = 88.7%). The model maintained high performance in leave-one-dataset-out validation (AUC = 0.90-0.93), demonstrating generalizability across unseen data from differing sites. A label-shuffling permutation test confirmed that the feature set reflects genuine neuroanatomical signal rather than statistical artifacts (p < 0.001). Conclusion This study demonstrates a robust, multi-site validated set of structural biomarkers associated with schizophrenia, enabling highly accurate case-control classification. The identified feature set provides a candidate neurobiological benchmark to inform and validate future deep learning models for automated diagnostic support in psychiatry, while acknowledging the need for future multi-diagnostic validation to establish differential diagnostic utility.

title: Gray matter subtyping with SuStaIn reveals neuroanatomical patterns in autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heterogeneous, and structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported both increased and decreased gray matter volume relative to typically developing controls. This variability may obscure distinct neuroanatomical patterns in conventional group-level analyses. It therefore motivates subtyping approaches that can characterize neuroanatomical heterogeneity beyond conventional group-level analyses. We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) to structural MRI data from the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) to identify gray matter subtypes and stage-like variation in ASD. Original and sign-reversed z-score representations were modeled to capture gray matter deviations above and below the control reference. We then evaluated whether the organization of subtype-related brain regions was consistent across deviation directions. Cross-direction consistency, within-ABIDE cross-cohort separability, and structural covariance network (SCN) differences between stage groups were assessed using subtype alignment, Dice coefficients, cross-cohort machine-learning classification, and structural covariance analyses. We identified two gray matter subtype patterns in ASD that were consistent across deviation directions. Subtype 1 was centered on cerebellar-limbic-striatal regions, whereas Subtype 2 involved anterior fronto-cingulo-insular regions. In exploratory covariate-adjusted analyses, higher stage in sign-reversed-model S1 was associated with lower verbal intelligence quotient (IQ) scores, whereas S2 showed modestly higher Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) scores. The two subtypes showed regionally distinct volume profiles. The two-subtype solution showed strong cross-direction agreement, and within-ABIDE cross-cohort classification supported structural separability of the aligned subtypes. In the sign-reversed model, SCN analyses further identified stage-group structural covariance differences within each subtype, with little evidence for a stable covariance difference between subtypes. This study identifies two gray matter-based ASD subtype patterns that were consistent across the original and sign-reversed z-score representations, with distinct regional volume profiles, selective clinical associations, and stage-group structural covariance differences. The findings provide a neuroanatomical framework for organizing ASD heterogeneity and for examining brain-behavior variation in future studies.

title: Multimodal MRI markers of white matter hyperintensities and their impact on cognition in cerebral small vessel disease: a systematic review.
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a leading cause of stroke, dementia, and age-related cognitive decline, with white matter hyperintensities (WMH) being a key imaging feature in MRI. This review aims to evaluate the association between multimodal magnetic resonance imaging markers of white matter hyperintensities and cognition in cerebral small vessel disease. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science (2016-2026) was done. Studies involving adults with MRI visible CSVD markers who underwent MRI standardized cognitive assessment were eligible. Fifteen studies were included with a total of 5752 participants. Included studies used conventional and advanced MRI techniques to evaluate the association of WMH with cognitive function. The findings were synthesized narratively according to MRI techniques. Conventional MRI studies showed that greater WMH burden and CSVD severity were associated with poorer cognition, particularly processing speed and global cognition, with individual studies reporting β values of - 0.371 (p < 0.001) and - 0.363 (p < 0.001), with good predictive accuracy reported in one study (AUC = 0.800, 95% CI: 0.710-0.891). While Advanced MRI also showed associations with microstructural and microvascular damage in white matter and with reduced blood flow was associated with poorer cognitive performance, individual studies reported β values of 0.268-0.273, moderate-to-strong associations (r = 0.310-0.441), good diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.86-0.89), and significantly lower scores on cognitive assessments (Mini-Mental State Examination: p < 0.001; Montreal Cognitive Assessment: p < 0.05). These findings suggest that WMH burden and disrupted white matter microstructure are associated with cognitive impairment. Larger, standardized studies are needed to determine the clinical value of MRI markers as reliable biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of cognitive impairment in CSVD.

title: Surgeons and Experts' Perspectives in Concomitant Bariatric Surgery with Cholecystectomy: Bari-Chole Egypt Survey.
abstract: The management of gallbladder disease during metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) remains controversial. Cholelithiasis is common in patients with obesity, yet the approach to concomitant or prophylactic cholecystectomy varies, with limited data from Egypt. This study aimed to assess Egyptian bariatric surgeons' practices, attitudes, and decision-making regarding cholecystectomy during MBS. A national cross-sectional survey was distributed to bariatric surgeons in Egypt, collecting information on demographics, surgical experience, preoperative screening, intraoperative decision-making, postoperative management, and prophylactic practices. The questionnaire included structured, closed-ended questions. Data were analyzed descriptively and compared between IFSO members and non-members using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant. A total of 117 surgeons participated, predominantly male (99%), with 16.2% IFSO members. Bariatric surgery was concentrated in Cairo (42%) and Alexandria (26%). Most surgeons (97%) screened gallstones preoperatively using abdominal ultrasound. Concomitant cholecystectomy was preferred for documented gallstones by 78%, while 82% never performed prophylactic cholecystectomy in patients with normal gallbladders. The majority performed the bariatric procedure first (82%) in reverse Trendelenburg position (88%), minimizing additional ports. Routine intraoperative cholangiography was rare (1.7%). Postoperative management largely mirrored isolated bariatric surgery, although antibiotic and drain practices differed between groups. Surgeons generally perceived combined procedures as safe, with 76% reporting no increase in complications and 89% reporting similar length of stay. Egyptian bariatric surgeons consistently screen for gallstones and favor concomitant cholecystectomy for documented stones, while largely avoiding prophylactic removal of normal gallbladders. Variation exists in intraoperative management and postoperative care. These findings highlight areas for standardization and support the development of a national pathway and multicenter registry to optimize gallbladder management in MBS.

title: Automated CT-based quantification of knee osteophytes for robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a multi-cohort study.
abstract: Preoperative computed tomography (CT) is routinely acquired for planning robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA), yet osteophyte burden is not quantitatively characterized. We developed automated CT-based osteophyte quantification and evaluated it against blinded de novo expert-consensus annotations and an intraoperative accessible resected osteophyte volume reference. A human-in-the-loop 3-dimensional U-Net was developed using 387 knee CT scans. The frozen model was evaluated against blinded de novo expert-consensus annotations in two independent external cohorts (100 knees each). Spatial and volume agreement were assessed using Dice coefficient, surface Dice at 1-mm tolerance, 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), mean absolute error, and Bland-Altman analysis. In a prospective cohort of 66 robotic-assisted TKAs, CT-derived total osteophyte volume was compared with the water-displacement volume of accessible osteophytes that were resected and recovered intraoperatively (accessible resected osteophyte volume reference). In the external cohorts, median total Dice was 0.913 and 0.909, surface Dice was 0.944 and 0.945, HD95 was 1.16 and 1.09 mm, and volume ICC was 0.977 and 0.972, respectively. Automated estimates showed conservative volume bias relative to expert consensus (- 0.499 and - 0.365 cc). In the surgical cohort, automated CT-derived volume showed cohort-level agreement with the accessible resected osteophyte volume reference (ICC, 0.876; mean absolute error, 1.224 cc; mean difference, + 0.401 cc; 95% limits of agreement, - 2.785 to + 3.586 cc). Automated CT-based osteophyte quantification showed consistent spatial and volumetric agreement with blinded de novo expert-consensus annotations across two external cohorts and cohort-level agreement with the accessible resected osteophyte volume reference. This scalable method provides a preoperative measure of osteophyte burden for arthroplasty research.

title: The clinical application value of mixed reality guidance in robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy for renal cancer.
abstract: Although robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy (RAL-RN) has realized the benefits of minimally invasive surgery, it continues to face several key technical limitations, including the lack of integrated patient-specific three-dimensional anatomical navigation and insufficient real-time intraoperative navigation. While mixed reality (MR) technology has shown considerable potential in renal tumor surgery, its clinical application value specifically within the context of radical nephrectomy for renal cancer warrants further systematic evaluation. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and practical value of MR guidance in RAL-RN. A retrospective analysis was conducted of 74 patients who underwent RAL-RN between September 2021 and March 2024. Participants were categorized into two groups based on preoperative assessment methodology: an MR navigation group (n = 33) and a conventional imaging group (n = 41). All patients received non-contrast and triple-phase contrast-enhanced renal CT scans. The MR group utilized Hololens-based intraoperative anatomical reference with three-dimensional models reconstructed from preoperative CT data during Da Vinci robotic procedures. Perioperative outcomes, including baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, operative time, estimated blood loss, and postoperative complications, were compared between the two groups to assess the potential technical advantages of MR-guided navigation. The two groups showed comparable baseline characteristics (p > 0.05). The MR group exhibited significantly shorter operative time (161.15 ± 10.87 min versus 182.29 ± 12.40 min, p < 0.001), reduced blood loss (150.00 mL [interquartile range 140.00 to 165.00] versus 165.00 mL [150.00 to 165.00], p = 0.008), faster gastrointestinal function recovery (26.82 ± 4.17 h versus 28.93 ± 3.68 h, p = 0.024), earlier tube removal (5.00 days [4.00 to 5.00] versus 6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00], p < 0.001), and shorter postoperative hospitalization (6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00] versus 8.00 days [7.00 to 8.00], p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in tumor staging, renal function parameters (postoperative and 12-month Scr and GFR), histopathological type, or complication rates (Clavien-Dindo grades 1 and 2) between groups (all p > 0.05). MR guidance was associated with shorter operative time and faster postoperative recovery in RAL-RN. However, given the non-randomized design, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and cannot establish causality. Prospective studies with standardized allocation and adequate follow-up are warranted to confirm the clinical value of MR guidance.

title: Residual congestion and urinary sodium and chloride trajectories in acute heart failure.
abstract: Residual congestion remains frequent after initial treatment for acute heart failure (AHF), and its presence may not be adequately identified using individual clinical or biochemical markers. We investigated residual congestion using a multimodal approach and examined its relationship with changes in urinary sodium and chloride during the first 72 h of hospitalization. We prospectively included consecutive patients hospitalized for AHF who underwent congestion assessment at admission and 72 h. Clinical evaluation, NT-proBNP, and venous Doppler ultrasound (VExUS) were integrated to assess congestion. Residual multimodal congestion was defined by the presence of at least two of three criteria: VExUS score ≥ 1, < 30% reduction in NT-proBNP, and clinical congestion score ≥ 3. Urinary sodium and chloride were measured at admission and 72 h, and their changes over time were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. Baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), worsening renal function, and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio were additionally characterized. Among 146 patients, 67 (45.9%) had residual multimodal congestion at 72 h. Urinary sodium and chloride concentrations were lower in patients with residual congestion. Both electrolytes decreased during the first 72 h (p < 0.001 for both), but their changes differed according to residual congestion status, with significant time-by-group interactions for sodium (p = 0.013) and chloride (p = 0.001). Patients with residual congestion also showed a trend toward poorer 180-day event-free survival, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank p = 0.078). Patients with residual congestion showed different early patterns of urinary sodium and chloride during treatment for AHF. Serial measurement of these electrolytes may complement clinical, biochemical, and venous ultrasound assessment when evaluating the response to decongestive therapy. These findings support their potential role in characterizing different decongestive profiles, although their clinical and prognostic value requires further evaluation.

title: The role of low muscle strength in predicting mortality in patients with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Sarcopenia is a prevalent complication in chronic liver disease (CLD), traditionally assessed by muscle mass. Recent paradigm shifts focus to dynapenia as the primary determinant of adverse outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the role of dynapenia, as measured by handgrip strength (HGS) and ultrasound-derived diaphragmatic excursion, in predicting mortality in this population. This prospective study included consecutive outpatients with cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma history attending a tertiary hepatology unit. Muscle mass was assessed in subgroups using bioimpedance analysis (BIA) and computed tomography (CT). Associations between sarcopenia proxies and 24-month all-cause mortality were analyzed with adjusted Cox regression models, and survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves. Ninety-one patients were included (age 73.4 ± 8.1 years; 71 [78%] male); 20 (22%) had dynapenia. Twenty-two deaths occurred at two years (24.2%). Over 24 months, dynapenia (by HGS) and diaphragmatic excursion were associated with mortality in adjusted models (aHR 1.68, 95% CI 1.12-2.53, p = 0.012; aHR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97, p = 0.042). In subgroups, they remained the only muscle parameters associated with mortality, while muscle mass indices were not significant. Finally, Kaplan-Meier estimates showed lower 24-month survival in dynapenic patients across groups (in overall population 65% vs. 79%, p = 0.05). Low muscle strength is a key prognostic parameter in patients with cirrhosis and HCC. In our small cohort, it was the only muscle-related measure significantly associated with mortality. These findings support further evaluation of muscle strength assessment as a potential tool for risk stratification in this population.

title: Diagnostic performance and timeliness of ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy for peripheral lymphadenopathy in Internal Medicine: a multicenter real-world study.
abstract: Background Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy (CNB) is increasingly used for evaluating peripheral lymphadenopathy, but evidence regarding its implementation in Internal Medicine remains limited. We assessed its diagnostic performance, safety, and diagnostic timeliness in routine clinical practice. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included consecutive patients undergoing ultrasound-guided CNB of peripheral lymphadenopathy in five Internal Medicine departments between February 2021 and March 2026. The primary outcome was diagnostic performance. Secondary outcomes included safety, diagnostic timeliness, performance in lymphoma patients, and factors associated with obtaining a definitive diagnosis. title: Impact of antithrombotic therapy on management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for upper gastrointestinal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Antithrombotic agents are frequently implicated in upper gastrointestinal bleeding (UGIB), yet their impact on prognosis and management remains unclear. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of pre-existing antithrombotic therapy on the management and prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB. Methods This study used data from a retrospective, multicenter cohort of adult patients hospitalized for UGIB between January 2019 and December 2020 in Greater Paris University Hospitals. Patients were categorized into four groups according to their pre-existing antithrombotic treatment: antiplatelet therapy, anticoagulant therapy, both, or none. The primary outcome was thirty-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included endoscopy, endoscopic hemostasis, and blood transfusion within 7 days, and intensive care unit admission. Associations were assessed using multivariable logistic regression and reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Results Among 928 patients, 226 (24%) were on antiplatelet therapy alone, 154 (17%) on anticoagulant therapy alone, 61 (7%) on combined therapy, and 487 (52%) received no antithrombotic treatment. Thirty-day mortality was 6.9%: 8.4% in the no-antithrombotic group, 6.2% in the antiplatelet group, 4.5% in the anticoagulant group, and 3.3% in the combined therapy group. Compared with the no-antithrombotic group, anticoagulant therapy alone was associated with lower mortality (aOR=0.28, 95% CI 0.10-0.83), while antiplatelet therapy alone or combined therapy were not significantly associated (aOR=0.47, 95% CI 0.19-1.14 and aOR=0.12, 95% CI 0.01-1.11, respectively). Neither anticoagulant nor antiplatelet therapy was associated with secondary outcomes. Conclusions Antithrombotic therapy had no negative impact on the management or prognosis of patients hospitalized for UGIB.

title: Accuracy of deep learning in quantifying epicardial adipose tissue: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) is significantly associated with cardiovascular disease and poor prognosis. Deep learning (DL) models have been explored for automatic EAT segmentation, but systematic evidence verifying their effectiveness is currently lacking. We conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and quantification, aiming to support the development of automated tools. We searched the Cochrane Library, Embase, Web of Science, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore through February 20, 2026. Studies reporting DL-based quantitative EAT segmentation were included. Quality was assessed with QUADAS-2. The Dice similarity coefficient (Dice), correlation coefficient (R), and Bland-Altman bias were used to evaluate segmentation efficacy, the correlation between automated segmentation and reference standards, and consistency, respectively. A random-effects model with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman method pooled these measures. Thirty eligible studies were included, covering five image types. For non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), the pooled Dice was 0.888 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.853-0.924), and the pooled R reached 0.973 (95%CI: 0.958-0.982). The contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) subgroup performed best, yielding a Dice of 0.910 (95% CI: 0.881-0.939) and an R of 0.989 (95% CI: 0.976-0.995). This meta-analysis quantifies the accuracy of DL models for EAT segmentation and volume quantification. The findings indicate that DL achieves robust accuracy on both NCCT and CECT images. However, given that most current studies rely on internal validation, future work should prioritize large-scale, multicenter external validation to support the translation of these promising DL tools into robust clinical diagnostic systems.
